title.zh: 卷二百十八 列傳第一百〇六 申時行 王錫爵 沈一貫 方從哲 沈㴶
title.en: Volume 218 Biographies 106: Shen Shixing, Wang Xijue, Shen Yiguan, Fang Congzhe, Shen Que
title.raw: 卷二百十八 列傳第一百〇六 申時行 王錫爵 沈一貫 方從哲 沈㴶 Volume 218 Biographies 106: Shen Shixing, Wang Xijue, Shen Yiguan, Fang Congzhe, Shen Que

sentences.zh: 申時行子 用懋 用嘉 孫 紹芳王錫爵弟 鼎爵 子 衡沈一貫 方從哲 沈㴶弟 演

translations.literal: Shen Shixing's sons Yongmao and Yongjia, grandson Shaofang; Wang Xijue's brother Dingjue's son Heng; Shen Yiguan; Fang Congzhe; Shen Que's brother Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing's sons Yongmao and Yongjia, his grandson Shaofang; Wang Xijue's brother Dingjue's son Heng; Shen Yiguan; Fang Congzhe; and Shen Que's brother Yan.

sentences.zh: 申時行

translations.literal: Shen Shixing
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing

sentences.zh: 申時行，字汝默，長洲人。

translations.literal: Shen Shixing, styled Rumo, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing, whose style name was Rumo, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十一年進士第一。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Jiajing he ranked first among jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 41 he took first place in the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 授修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 歷左庶子，掌翰林院事。

translations.literal: He successively served as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and managed affairs of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and director of Hanlin Academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年，由禮部右侍郎改吏部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli, he was transferred from Right Vice Minister of Rites to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 he was moved from Right Vice Minister of Rites to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時行以文字受知張居正，蘊藉不立崖異，居正安之。

translations.literal: Shixing had won Zhang Juzheng's favor through his literary talent; restrained and unostentatious, he did not set himself apart, and Juzheng was at ease with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing had impressed Zhang Juzheng with his writing; mild and unassuming, he never struck a pose, and Juzheng trusted him.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，居正將歸葬父，請廣閣臣，遂以左侍郎兼東閣大學士入預機務。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year, as Juzheng was about to return home to bury his father, he requested an expansion of the Grand Secretaries; Shixing was thus made Left Vice Minister concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Wanli 6, when Juzheng was preparing to go home for his father's funeral, he asked that the Grand Secretariat be enlarged; Shixing was appointed Left Vice Minister and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion to join in deliberating policy.

sentences.zh: 已，進禮部尚書兼文淵閣，累進少傅兼太子太傅、吏部尚書、建極殿。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was promoted to Minister of Rites concurrently of the Wenyuan Pavilion, and was successively advanced to Junior Tutor concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Jianji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Minister of Rites with a seat in the Wenyuan Pavilion, and later rose step by step to Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Jianji Hall.

sentences.zh: 張居正攬權久，操群下如束濕，異己者率逐去之。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng had long monopolized power and controlled his subordinates as tightly as binding wet rope; those who differed from him were generally driven away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng had held power for years and kept officials on as short a leash as wet cord; anyone who crossed him was usually expelled.

sentences.zh: 及居正卒，張四維、時行相繼柄政，務為寬大。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, Zhang Siwei and Shixing succeeded each other in wielding power, striving for leniency in policy.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death, Zhang Siwei and then Shixing took the helm in turn, both aiming at a softer style of rule.

sentences.zh: 以次收召老成，布列庶位，朝論多稱之。

translations.literal: They gradually recalled experienced officials in turn and filled various posts; court opinion largely praised them.
translations.idiomatic: They slowly brought back seasoned men and spread them through the ranks, and public opinion in the capital largely approved.

sentences.zh: 然是時內閣權積重，六卿大抵徇閣臣指。

translations.literal: Yet at this time the accumulated weight of inner-cabinet authority meant the Six Ministers mostly followed the Grand Secretaries' directions.
translations.idiomatic: By then, however, the Grand Secretariat had grown so powerful that the heads of the six ministries mostly did as the Grand Secretaries wished.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣由四維、時行起，樂其寬，多與相厚善。

translations.literal: The grand ministers had risen under Siwei and Shixing and, pleased with their leniency, mostly became close allies with them.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials who had advanced under Siwei and Shixing welcomed their easy manner and for the most part stood with them as friends.

sentences.zh: 四維憂歸，時行為首輔。

translations.literal: When Siwei went into mourning and left office, Shixing became chief Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Siwei left for mourning, Shixing became chief among the Grand Secretaries.

sentences.zh: 余有丁、許國、王錫爵、王家屏先後同居政府，無嫌猜。

translations.literal: Yu Youding, Xu Guo, Wang Xijue, and Wang Jiaping successively served together in the government without suspicion or friction.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Youding, Xu Guo, Wang Xijue, and Wang Jiaping served together in the cabinet in succession, without jealousy or quarrel.

sentences.zh: 而言路為居正所遏，至是方發舒。

translations.literal: The remonstrance officials had been suppressed under Juzheng; only now did they begin to flourish again.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial and remonstrance corps had been muzzled under Juzheng; now at last they found their voice again.

sentences.zh: 以居正素昵時行，不能無諷刺。

translations.literal: Because Juzheng had been on intimate terms with Shixing, they could not refrain from sarcastic remarks.
translations.idiomatic: Since Juzheng had favored Shixing, the remonstrators could not help aiming barbed comments at him as well.

sentences.zh: 時行外示博大能容人，心故弗善也。

translations.literal: Shixing outwardly displayed great breadth and capacity to tolerate others, yet in his heart he was not truly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing put on a show of magnanimity, but inwardly he bore them no goodwill.

sentences.zh: 帝雖樂言者訐居正短，而頗惡人論時事，言事者間謫官。

translations.literal: Though the emperor enjoyed hearing critics enumerate Juzheng's failings, he also greatly disliked people discussing current affairs; those who spoke on policy were occasionally demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor liked to hear Juzheng attacked, yet he hated open debate on current affairs; remonstrators who crossed that line were sometimes punished with demotion.

sentences.zh: 眾以此望時行，口語相詆諆。

translations.literal: Many therefore pinned hopes on Shixing, and verbal abuse mutually slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Many looked to Shixing for relief, even as factions traded insults in speech.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣又皆右時行拄言者口，言者益憤，時行以此損物望。

translations.literal: The grand ministers also largely sided with Shixing to muzzle the remonstrators; the remonstrators grew angrier, and Shixing thereby lost public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers mostly backed Shixing against the remonstrators; the remonstrators only grew fiercer, and Shixing's reputation suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，御史張文熙嘗言前閣臣專恣者四事，請帝永禁革之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year, Censor Zhang Wenxi had urged four matters in which former Grand Secretaries had acted arbitrarily, asking the emperor permanently to forbid and abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Wanli 12, Censor Zhang Wenxi listed four abuses by past Grand Secretaries and asked that the throne forbid them forever.

sentences.zh: 時行疏爭曰：「文熙謂部院百執事不當置考成簿，送閣察考；

translations.literal: Shixing memorialized in rebuttal, saying: "Wenxi holds that the hundred officials of the ministries and directorates should not be entered on the performance-assessment register sent to the Grand Secretariat for review;
translations.idiomatic: Shixing protested in a memorial: "Wenxi says that the hundred-odd officials of the ministries and directorates must not be listed on the kao-cheng assessment books sent to the Grand Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 吏、兵二部除授，不當一一取裁；

translations.literal: that appointments by the Ministries of Personnel and War should not be decided one by one by the Grand Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: that the Ministries of Personnel and War should not have every appointment subject to Grand Secretariat approval;

sentences.zh: 督撫巡按行事，不當密揭請教；

translations.literal: that governors-general, grand coordinators, and touring censors should not report in secret memorials for instruction;
translations.idiomatic: that governors, grand coordinators, and touring censors should not send secret memorials asking how to act;

sentences.zh: 閣中票擬，當使同官知。

translations.literal: and that draft rescripts in the Grand Secretariat should be known to fellow Grand Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: and that draft rescripts in the Grand Secretariat should be shared with one's colleagues.

sentences.zh: 夫閣臣不職當罷黜，若並其執掌盡削之，是因噎廢食也。

translations.literal: If Grand Secretaries are unfit for office they should be dismissed; but to strip them of all their functions at once is to give up eating for fear of choking.
translations.idiomatic: Unworthy Grand Secretaries ought to be removed—but to abolish all their duties at once is to throw away food because one once choked.

sentences.zh: 至票擬，無不與同官議者。

translations.literal: As for draft rescripts, there is none that is not discussed with fellow Grand Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: As for drafting rescripts, nothing is done without consulting the other Grand Secretaries."

sentences.zh: 」帝深以為然，絀文熙議不用。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved, and demoted Wenxi's proposal without adopting it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed and set Wenxi's proposal aside without adopting it.

sentences.zh: 御史丁此呂言侍郎高啟愚以試題勸進居正，帝手疏示時行。

translations.literal: Censor Ding Cilü said that Vice Minister Gao Qiyu, in an examination question, had urged advancing Juzheng; the emperor wrote a personal rescript and showed it to Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ding Cilü charged that Vice Minister Gao Qiyu had used an examination topic to urge promoting Juzheng; the emperor drafted a note in his own hand and showed it to Shixing.

sentences.zh: 時行曰：「此呂以曖昧陷人大辟，恐讒言接踵至，非清明之朝所宜有。

translations.literal: Shixing said: "Cilü, on the basis of ambiguous wording, would trap a man in the gravest penalty; I fear slander will follow in waves—this is not what a clear-sighted court should allow."
translations.idiomatic: Shixing said: "Cilü would send a man to death on vague insinuation; if that stands, calumny will come in waves—no clear court should permit it."

sentences.zh: 」尚書楊巍因請出此呂於外，帝從巍言。

translations.literal: Minister Yang Wei therefore asked that Cilü be sent outside the capital; the emperor followed Wei's advice.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yang Wei asked that Cilü be posted away from the capital, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 而給事御史王士性、李植等交章劾巍阿時行意，蔽塞言路。

translations.literal: But Supervising Secretaries and censors Wang Shixing, Li Zhi, and others jointly memorialized that Wei was currying favor with Shixing and blocking the remonstrance route.
translations.idiomatic: Yet supervising secretaries and censors such as Wang Shixing and Li Zhi submitted joint memorials accusing Wei of pandering to Shixing and choking off free speech.

sentences.zh: 帝尋亦悔之，命罷啟愚，留此呂。

translations.literal: The emperor soon regretted it and ordered that Qiyu be dismissed but Cilü retained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon regretted his decision and ordered Qiyu dismissed while keeping Cilü in office.

sentences.zh: 時行、巍求去。

translations.literal: Shixing and Wei asked to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing and Wei both asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 有丁、國言：「大臣國體所系，今以群言留此呂，恐無以安時行、巍心。

translations.literal: Youding and Guo said: "Grand ministers are bound up with the dignity of the state; if the multitude's words keep Cilü, I fear Shixing and Wei will have no peace of mind."
translations.idiomatic: Youding and Guo argued: "Grand ministers embody the state's dignity; if popular clamor keeps Cilü, Shixing and Wei cannot feel secure in their posts."

sentences.zh: 」國尤不勝憤，專疏求去，詆諸言路。

translations.literal: Guo was especially unable to contain his anger and submitted a separate memorial asking to leave, reviling the remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: Guo, unable to contain his anger, filed his own resignation memorial and lashed out at the remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 副都御史石星、侍郎陸光祖亦以為言。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Shi Xing and Vice Minister Lu Guangzu also spoke to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Shi Xing and Vice Minister Lu Guangzu made the same point.

sentences.zh: 帝乃聽巍，出此呂於外，慰留時行、國，而言路群起攻國。

translations.literal: The emperor then allowed Wei to go, sent Cilü outside the capital, and urged Shixing and Guo to stay; but the remonstrators rose as a body to attack Guo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then let Wei resign, posted Cilü outside the capital, and pressed Shixing and Guo to remain—whereupon the remonstrators turned on Guo in force.

sentences.zh: 時行請量罰言者，言者益心憾。

translations.literal: Shixing asked that the remonstrators be punished in proportion; they only resented him the more.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing asked that the remonstrators be punished in measure; they hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 既而李植、江東之以大峪山壽宮事撼時行不勝，貶去，閣臣與言路日相水火矣。

translations.literal: Before long Li Zhi and Jiang Dongzhi, on the matter of the Dayu Mountain mausoleum, shook Shixing but could not prevail and were demoted; Grand Secretaries and remonstrators were daily at loggerheads.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Zhi and Jiang Dongzhi attacked Shixing over the Dayu Mountain tomb project, failed, and were demoted; from then on the cabinet and the remonstrance corps were locked in open feud.

sentences.zh: 初，御史魏允貞、郎中李三才以科場事論及時行子用懋，貶官。

translations.literal: Earlier, Censor Wei Yunzhen and Director Li Sancai, on a matter of the civil-service examinations, had implicated Shixing's son Yongmao and been demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Censor Wei Yunzhen and Director Li Sancai, in a dispute over the examinations, had touched Shixing's son Yongmao and been demoted.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄒元標劾罷時行姻徐學謨，時行假他疏逐之去。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zou Yuanbiao had impeached and removed Shixing's in-law Xu Xuemo; Shixing used another memorial to drive him away.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zou Yuanbiao had impeached Shixing's kinsman by marriage Xu Xuemo out of office; Shixing then used another memorial to force Zou out as well.

sentences.zh: 已而占物情，稍稍擢三人官，三人得毋廢。

translations.literal: Later, gauging public sentiment, he gradually promoted the three men in rank, and the three were not ruined after all.
translations.idiomatic: Later, reading the mood of the times, he slowly restored the three men's offices, so they were not destroyed in the end.

sentences.zh: 世以此稱時行長者。

translations.literal: The age therefore called Shixing a man of forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries therefore praised Shixing as a man of forbearance.

sentences.zh: 時行欲收人心，罷居正時所行考成法；

translations.literal: Shixing wished to win hearts and abolished the performance-assessment system instituted under Juzheng;
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to win goodwill, Shixing abolished the kao-cheng performance reviews Juzheng had imposed;

sentences.zh: 一切為簡易，亦數有獻納。

translations.literal: he made everything simpler and easier, and also offered advice on several occasions.
translations.idiomatic: he simplified procedures across the board and several times offered constructive counsel.

sentences.zh: 嘗因災異，力言催科急迫，征派加增，刑獄繁多，用度侈靡之害。

translations.literal: On one occasion, citing natural disasters, he spoke forcefully of the harm of urgent tax collection, added levies, numerous punishments, and extravagant expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Once, invoking natural calamities, he spoke bluntly of the evils of harsh tax collection, extra levies, crowded prisons, and lavish spending.

sentences.zh: 又嘗請止撫按官助工贓罰銀，請減織造數，趣發諸司章奏。

translations.literal: He also asked that the contributions and fines imposed on grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners for construction projects be stopped, that the quotas for imperial textile manufacture be reduced, and that memorials from the ministries be expedited.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to end the "assistance" fines levied on provincial governors, to cut imperial silk quotas, and to speed up ministry memorials.

sentences.zh: 緣尚寶卿徐貞明議，請開畿內水田。

translations.literal: Following Court Gentleman Xu Zhenming's proposal, he asked to open paddy fields within the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Following Court Gentleman Xu Zhenming, he urged opening irrigated fields in the metropolitan districts.

sentences.zh: 用鄧子龍、劉綎平隴川，薦鄭洛為經略，趣順義王東歸，寢葉夢熊奏以弭楊應龍之變。

translations.literal: He employed Deng Zilong and Liu Ting to pacify Longchuan, recommended Zheng Luo as frontier commissioner, urged the Shunyi prince to return east, and shelved Ye Mengxiong's memorial to quiet the Yang Yinglong rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He used Deng Zilong and Liu Ting to pacify Longchuan, recommended Zheng Luo as frontier commissioner, pressed the Shunyi prince to return east, and set aside Ye Mengxiong's memorial to defuse the Yang Yinglong crisis.

sentences.zh: 然是時天下承平，上下恬熙，法紀漸不振。

translations.literal: Yet at this time the realm enjoyed peace; above and below were at ease, and law and discipline gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the empire was at peace; court and country were complacent, and discipline slowly slackened.

sentences.zh: 時行務承帝指，不能大有建立。

translations.literal: Shixing strove to follow the emperor's wishes and could not achieve great reforms.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing tried above all to follow the emperor's mind and accomplished little of lasting weight.

sentences.zh: 帝每遇講期，多傳免。

translations.literal: Whenever lecture day came, the emperor often excused himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the day came for the classics lecture, the emperor often sent word that he would not attend.

sentences.zh: 時行請雖免講，仍進講章。

translations.literal: Shixing asked that even when lectures were excused, the lecture chapters still be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing asked that even when lectures were canceled, the prepared lecture texts still be presented.

sentences.zh: 自後為故事，講筵遂永罷。

translations.literal: Thereafter this became precedent, and the lecture hall was permanently abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: That became the custom thereafter, and the lecture hall was abandoned for good.

sentences.zh: 評事雒於仁進《酒色財氣四箴》，帝大怒，召時行等條分析之，將重譴。

translations.literal: Reviewer Luo Yuren submitted the Four Admonitions on wine, sex, wealth, and temper; the emperor was furious and summoned Shixing and others to analyze them item by item, intending severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewer Luo Yuren presented his Four Admonitions on wine, sex, wealth, and temper; the emperor was furious, summoned Shixing and the others to parse each point, and prepared heavy penalties.

sentences.zh: 時行請毋下其章，而諷於仁自引去，於仁賴以免。

translations.literal: Shixing asked that the memorial not be circulated and hinted that Yuren withdraw of his own accord; Yuren was spared thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing asked that the memorial not be published and quietly urged Yuren to resign; Yuren escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 然章奏留中自此始。

translations.literal: Yet from this time memorials held back at court began.
translations.idiomatic: From that time, however, the practice began of keeping memorials at the palace without action.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，光宗年五歲，而鄭貴妃有寵，生皇三子常洵，頗萌奪嫡意。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year, the Guangzong heir was five years old, while Consort Zheng was favored and had borne the third imperial son Changxun; the idea of displacing the heir began to stir.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Wanli 14, Heir Apparent Guangzong was only five, but favored Consort Zheng had borne the third son Changxun, and talk of replacing the heir began to circulate.

sentences.zh: 時行率同列再請建儲，不聽。

translations.literal: Shixing led his colleagues in again requesting the establishment of an heir; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing led the Grand Secretariat in again urging that the heir be named; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 廷臣以貴妃故，多指斥宮闈，觸帝怒，被嚴譴。

translations.literal: Court officials, because of the consort, mostly criticized the inner palace; they provoked the emperor's anger and were severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials, because of the consort, attacked the inner palace; the emperor's wrath fell on them and they were harshly punished.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗詔求直言。

translations.literal: The emperor once issued an edict calling for blunt speech.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once issued an edict inviting frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 郎官劉復初、李懋檜等顯侵貴妃。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen Liu Fuchu, Li Maojian, and others openly attacked the consort.
translations.idiomatic: Court gentlemen Liu Fuchu and Li Maojian openly assailed the consort.

sentences.zh: 時行請帝下詔，令諸曹建言止及所司職掌，聽其長擇而獻之，不得專達。

translations.literal: Shixing asked the emperor to issue an edict ordering all offices to limit memorials to their own duties, to let their superiors select and submit them, and not to send them directly.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing asked the emperor to decree that every office confine memorials to its own jurisdiction, let chiefs choose what to forward, and forbid direct submission to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅，眾多咎時行者。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; many blamed Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted; many held Shixing responsible.

sentences.zh: 時行連請建儲。

translations.literal: Shixing repeatedly asked for the establishment of an heir.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing again and again pressed for investiture of the heir.

sentences.zh: 十八年，帝召皇長子、皇三子，令時行入見毓德宮。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the emperor summoned the eldest imperial son and the third son and had Shixing enter to see them in the Yude Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 18 the emperor summoned the eldest prince and the third prince and had Shixing received at the Yude Palace.

sentences.zh: 時行拜賀，請亟定大計。

translations.literal: Shixing bowed in congratulation and asked that the great decision be settled quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing bowed in congratulation and begged that the succession be settled at once.

sentences.zh: 帝猶豫久之，下詔曰：「朕不喜激聒。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated for a long time and issued an edict saying: "I dislike vehement remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated a long time, then issued an edict: "I dislike shrill remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 近諸臣章奏概留中，惡其離間朕父子。

translations.literal: Recently the ministers' memorials have all been held at court, because I detest their driving a wedge between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I have held back your memorials because I hate your driving a wedge between father and son.

sentences.zh: 若明歲廷臣不復瀆擾，當以後年冊立，否則俟皇長子十五歲舉行。

translations.literal: If next year the court officials do not harass me again, I will invest the heir the year after; otherwise I will wait until the eldest son is fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: If next year the court does not pester me again, I will invest the heir the year after; otherwise I will wait until the eldest son is fifteen."

sentences.zh: 」時行因戒廷臣毋激擾。

translations.literal: Shixing therefore warned the court officials not to provoke disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing then warned the court not to stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，工部主事張有德請具冊立儀註。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year, Director Zhang Youde of the Ministry of Works asked that the investiture ceremonies be drawn up.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the next year, Zhang Youde of the Ministry of Works asked that investiture rites be prepared.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命展期一年。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered the deadline extended by one year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and postponed the date by a year.

sentences.zh: 而內閣中亦有疏入。

translations.literal: Yet within the Grand Secretariat there was also a memorial submitted.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial from within the Grand Secretariat had also gone in.

sentences.zh: 時行方在告，次輔國首列時行名。

translations.literal: Shixing was then on leave; the acting chief Guo listed Shixing's name first.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing was on leave at the time; Acting Chief Guo put Shixing's name at the head of the memorial.

sentences.zh: 時行密上封事，言：「臣方在告，初不預知。

translations.literal: Shixing secretly submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "I am on leave and knew nothing of this at first.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing sent a secret memorial saying: "I was on leave and knew nothing of this at first.

sentences.zh: 冊立之事，聖意已定。

translations.literal: The matter of investiture—the sacred mind is already decided.
translations.idiomatic: On investiture, Your Majesty's mind is already made up.

sentences.zh: 有德不諳大計，惟宸斷親裁，勿因小臣妨大典。

translations.literal: Youde does not understand the great plan; let Your Majesty decide personally and do not let a minor official obstruct a great ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: Youde does not grasp the larger design; let Your Majesty decide alone and do not let a minor official block a great state ceremony."

sentences.zh: 」於是給事中羅大纮劾時行，謂陽附群臣之議以請立，而陰緩其事以內交。

translations.literal: Thereupon Supervising Secretary Luo Dahong impeached Shixing, saying he outwardly joined the ministers in asking for investiture while inwardly delaying the matter to curry favor within.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Luo Dahong then impeached Shixing, charging that he publicly backed investiture while privately slowing it to win favor inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 中書黃正賓復論時行排陷同官，巧避首事之罪。

translations.literal: Secretary Huang Zhengbin again accused Shixing of framing his colleagues and cleverly evading responsibility as the chief initiator.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Huang Zhengbin accused Shixing of trapping colleagues and dodging blame as the prime mover.

sentences.zh: 二人皆被黜責。

translations.literal: Both men were dismissed and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Both were dismissed and punished.

sentences.zh: 御史鄒德泳疏復上，時行力求罷。

translations.literal: Censor Zou Deyong submitted another memorial; Shixing strove to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zou Deyong memorialized again; Shixing pressed hard to resign.

sentences.zh: 詔馳驛歸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him home by relay post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent him home by imperial courier.

sentences.zh: 歸三年，光宗始出閣講學，十年始立為皇太子。

translations.literal: Three years after his return, Guangzong was at last brought out of the palace for lectures; ten years later he was finally invested as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after Shixing left, Guangzong was finally brought out for instruction; ten years passed before he was invested crown prince.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，時行年八十，帝遣行人存問。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year Shixing was eighty; the emperor sent a courier to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 42, when Shixing was eighty, the emperor sent an envoy to ask after him.

sentences.zh: 詔書至門而卒。

translations.literal: The edict reached his gate as he died.
translations.idiomatic: The edict arrived at his gate the day he died.

sentences.zh: 先以雲南嶽鳳平，加少師兼太子太師、中極殿大學士，詔贈太師，謚文定。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Yue Feng had been pacified in Yunnan, he had been advanced to Junior Tutor concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Zhongji Hall; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wendi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Yue Feng's pacification in Yunnan, he had been promoted to Junior Tutor, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Grand Secretary of the Zhongji Hall; he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wendi.

sentences.zh: 子 用懋 用嘉

translations.literal: Sons Yongmao and Yongjia
translations.idiomatic: Sons Yongmao and Yongjia

sentences.zh: 子用懋、用嘉。

translations.literal: His sons Yongmao and Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yongmao and Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 用懋，字敬中，舉進士。

translations.literal: Yongmao, styled Jingzhong, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yongmao, style name Jingzhong, became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 累官兵部職方郎中。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director in the Ministry of War's Bureau of Operations.

sentences.zh: 神宗擢太仆少卿，仍視職方事。

translations.literal: The Shenzong promoted him to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud while he still oversaw Bureau of Operations affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong promoted him to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud while he still handled operations work.

sentences.zh: 再遷右僉都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，歷兵部左、右侍郎，拜尚書，致仕歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he successively served as Left and Right Vice Minister of War, was appointed Minister, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen he served as Left and Right Vice Minister of War, became Minister, and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 用嘉，舉人。

translations.literal: Yongjia passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 歷官廣西參政。

translations.literal: He successively served as Administrative Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administrative commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 孫 紹芳

translations.literal: Grandson Shaofang
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Shaofang

sentences.zh: 孫紹芳，進士，戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Shaofang, a jinshi, became Left Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shaofang, a jinshi, rose to Left Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 王錫爵

translations.literal: Wang Xijue
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xijue

sentences.zh: 王錫爵，字元馭，太倉人。

translations.literal: Wang Xijue, styled Yuanyu, was a native of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xijue, style name Yuanyu, came from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十一年舉會試第一，廷試第二，授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Jiajing he ranked first in the metropolitan examination and second in the palace examination, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 41 he placed first in the metropolitan exam and second in the palace exam, and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷至祭酒。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年，以詹事掌翰林院。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli, as Grand Mentor he managed the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 5 he served as Grand Mentor directing Hanlin Academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 張居正奪情，將廷杖吳中行、趙用賢等。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng seized mourning leave, he was about to have Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, and others beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng forced his way out of mourning, he planned to have Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, and others beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 錫爵要同館十餘人詣居正求解，居正不納。

translations.literal: Xijue asked more than ten fellow Hanlin members to go to Juzheng to plead for them; Juzheng would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue asked a dozen fellow academicians to beg Juzheng for mercy; Juzheng refused.

sentences.zh: 錫爵獨造喪次，切言之，居正徑入不顧。

translations.literal: Xijue alone went to the mourning lodge and spoke urgently; Juzheng went straight inside without heeding him.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue went alone to the mourning lodge and pleaded earnestly; Juzheng walked straight in and ignored him.

sentences.zh: 中行等既受杖，錫爵持之大慟。

translations.literal: After Zhongxing and the others had been beaten, Xijue held them and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongxing and the others had been flogged, Xijue held them and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 明年，進禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: The following year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 居正甫歸治喪，九卿急請召還，錫爵獨不署名。

translations.literal: Juzheng had just returned to observe mourning when the Nine Ministers urgently asked that he be recalled; Xijue alone did not sign.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng had barely gone home for mourning when the Nine Ministers urgently petitioned his recall; Xijue alone withheld his signature.

sentences.zh: 旋乞省親去。

translations.literal: Soon he asked leave to visit his parents and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to visit his parents and left office.

sentences.zh: 居正以錫爵形己短，益銜之，錫爵遂不出。

translations.literal: Juzheng, because Xijue had exposed his shortcomings, resented him all the more, and Xijue therefore did not return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng, feeling Xijue had shown up his faults, hated him the more, and Xijue stayed out of office.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，即家拜禮部尚書兼文淵閣大學士，參機務。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year, while at home he was appointed Minister of Rites concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Wanli 12 he was appointed from home as Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 還朝，請禁諂諛、抑奔競、戒虛浮、節侈靡、辟橫議、簡工作。

translations.literal: On returning to court he asked that flattery be forbidden, careerist scrambling curbed, empty show restrained, extravagance checked, reckless debate avoided, and construction projects simplified.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he urged bans on flattery, curbing of office-seeking, restraint of empty display, thrift, an end to reckless controversy, and simpler public works.

sentences.zh: 帝咸褒納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted every point.

sentences.zh: 初，李植、江東之與大臣申時行、楊巍等相構，以錫爵負時望，且與居正貳，力推之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Zhi and Jiang Dongzhi had contended with the grand ministers Shen Shixing and Yang Wei; because Xijue enjoyed public esteem and had differed from Juzheng, they strongly promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Zhi and Jiang Dongzhi had feuded with Shen Shixing, Yang Wei, and others; seeing Xijue's standing and his break with Juzheng, they pushed hard for him.

sentences.zh: 比錫爵至，與時行合，反出疏力排植等，植等遂去。

translations.literal: But when Xijue arrived he united with Shixing and instead issued memorials fiercely attacking Zhi and the others, who thereupon left office.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xijue arrived he sided with Shixing and memorialized fiercely against Zhi and his allies, who were driven out.

sentences.zh: 時時行為首輔，許國次之，三人皆南畿人，而錫爵與時行同舉會試，且同郡，政府相得甚。

translations.literal: At this time Shixing was chief Grand Secretary, with Xu Guo second; all three were from the southern metropolitan region, and Xijue had taken the metropolitan examination together with Shixing and was from the same prefecture—the government worked in close harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing was chief Grand Secretary, Xu Guo second; all three were Jiangnan men, and Xijue had passed the metropolitan exam with Shixing from the same county—the cabinet got on famously.

sentences.zh: 然時行柔和，而錫爵性剛負氣。

translations.literal: Yet Shixing was gentle, while Xijue was by nature stern and proud.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing was mild, but Xijue was proud and quick-tempered.

sentences.zh: 十六年，子衡舉順天試第一，郎官高桂、饒伸論之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year his son Heng took first place in the Shuntian provincial examination; court gentlemen Gao Gui and Rao Shen criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 16 his son Heng ranked first in the Shuntian provincial exam; court gentlemen Gao Gui and Rao Shen attacked the result.

sentences.zh: 錫爵連章辨訐，語過忿，伸坐下詔獄除名，桂謫邊方。

translations.literal: Xijue submitted successive memorials in rebuttal, his language excessively angry; Shen was imprisoned, removed from the roster, and Gui was banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue answered in a stream of angry memorials; Shen was jailed and struck from the rolls, and Gui was exiled.

sentences.zh: 御史喬璧星請帝戒諭錫爵，務擴其量，為休休有容之臣，錫爵疏辨。

translations.literal: Censor Qiao Bixing asked the emperor to admonish Xijue to broaden his measure and be a minister of easy tolerance; Xijue memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Qiao Bixing asked the emperor to warn Xijue to be more magnanimous; Xijue defended himself in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 以是積與廷論忤。

translations.literal: Thus he increasingly clashed with court opinion.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he clashed repeatedly with opinion at court.

sentences.zh: 時群臣請建儲者眾，帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: At this time many ministers asked that an heir be established; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials were pressing for investiture of the heir; the emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 十八年，錫爵疏請豫教元子，錄用言官姜應麟等，且求宥故巡撫李材，不報。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Xijue memorialized asking early instruction for the eldest son, reinstatement of remonstrance officials such as Jiang Yinglin, and pardon for the former grand coordinator Li Cai; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 18 Xijue asked early schooling for the eldest son, restoration of remonstrators like Jiang Yinglin, and pardon for ex-grand coordinator Li Cai—all unanswered.

sentences.zh: 嘗因旱災，自陳乞罷。

translations.literal: On one occasion, citing drought, he asked to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Once, citing drought, he offered to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔留之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict keeping him in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict keeping him on.

sentences.zh: 火落赤、真相犯西陲，議者爭請用兵，錫爵主款，與時行合。

translations.literal: Huoluo Chi and Zhenxiang invaded the western frontier; debaters clamored for war, but Xijue favored peace and agreed with Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huoluo Chi and Zhenxiang raided the western border, many urged war, but Xijue favored accommodation, as did Shixing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，偕同列爭冊立不得，杜門乞歸。

translations.literal: Before long, together with his colleagues he strove for investiture without success and shut his doors to ask to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and his colleagues failed again on investiture and begged to go home.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老，連乞歸省。

translations.literal: Soon, because his mother was old, he repeatedly asked to return and visit her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother being old, he soon asked repeatedly to visit her.

sentences.zh: 乃賜道里費，遣官護行。

translations.literal: He was granted traveling expenses and an escort was sent to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted traveling funds and sent an escort.

sentences.zh: 歸二年，時行、國及王家屏相繼去位，有詔趣召錫爵。

translations.literal: Two years after his return, Shixing, Guo, and Wang Jiaping left office in succession, and an edict urgently recalled Xijue.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, as Shixing, Guo, and Wang Jiaping left in turn, an edict hurried Xijue back.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月，還朝，遂為首輔。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year he returned to court and became chief Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Wanli 21 he returned and became chief Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 先是有旨，是年春舉冊立大典，戒廷臣毋瀆陳。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been an edict that the great investiture ceremony would be held that spring and that court officials were not to harass the throne with repeated memorials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had already fixed investiture for that spring and warned officials not to pester the throne.

sentences.zh: 廷臣鑒張有德事，咸默默。

translations.literal: Court officials, mindful of Zhang Youde's case, all kept silent.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Zhang Youde's punishment, the court fell silent.

sentences.zh: 及是，錫爵密請帝決大計。

translations.literal: At this juncture Xijue secretly asked the emperor to settle the great decision.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue then secretly urged the emperor to settle succession.

sentences.zh: 帝遣內侍以手詔示錫爵，欲待嫡子，令元子與兩弟且並封為王。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a eunuch with a personal edict showing Xijue that he wished to wait for a son of the empress and for the time being enfeoff the eldest son and his two brothers all as kings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a eunuch with a handwritten edict: he wished to wait for a son of the empress and meanwhile enfeoff the eldest son and his two brothers as kings.

sentences.zh: 錫爵懼失上指，立奉詔擬諭旨。

translations.literal: Xijue, fearing to miss the emperor's intent, immediately drafted a rescript to carry out the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid to miss the emperor's meaning, Xijue at once drafted a rescript to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 而又外慮公論，因言「漢明帝馬後、唐明皇王後、宋真宗劉後皆養諸妃子為子，請令皇后撫育元子，則元子即嫡子，而生母不必崇位號以上壓皇貴妃」，亦擬諭以進。

translations.literal: Yet he also feared public opinion and therefore said: "Emperor Ming of Han's Empress Ma, Emperor Ming of Tang's Empress Wang, and Emperor Zhenzong of Song's Empress Liu all raised sons of consorts as their own; let the empress nurture the eldest son, then the eldest son will be the legitimate son, and the birth mother need not be given a title that would rank above the honored consort"—he also drafted a rescript to this effect for submission.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing public outrage, he cited Han, Tang, and Song empresses who had raised other women's sons and proposed that the empress adopt the eldest son as her own so he would count as legitimate, without elevating his birth mother's title above the honored consort—he drafted that too.

sentences.zh: 同列趙誌臯、張位咸不預聞。

translations.literal: His colleagues Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei were both kept uninformed.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues Zhao Zhigao and Zhang Wei knew nothing of this.

sentences.zh: 帝竟以前諭下禮官，令即具儀。

translations.literal: The emperor at last sent the earlier instruction down to the Ministry of Rites, ordering them immediately to draw up the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the first order to the Ministry of Rites to prepare the rites at once.

sentences.zh: 於是舉朝大嘩。

translations.literal: Thereupon the whole court erupted.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court erupted in protest.

sentences.zh: 給事中史孟麟、禮部尚書羅萬化等，群詣錫爵第，力爭。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Shi Menglin, Minister of Rites Luo Wanhua, and others went in a body to Xijue's residence to argue fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Shi Menglin, Minister Luo Wanhua, and others marched on Xijue's house to protest.

sentences.zh: 廷臣諫者，章日數上。

translations.literal: Memorials of remonstrance from court officials came in daily.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance memorials poured in daily.

sentences.zh: 錫爵偕誌臯、位力請追還前詔，帝不從。

translations.literal: Xijue, with Zhigao and Wei, urgently asked that the earlier edict be withdrawn; the emperor would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue, Zhigao, and Wei begged to recall the edict; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 已而諫者益多，而嶽元聲、顧允成、張納陛、陳泰來、於孔兼、李啟美、曾鳳儀、鐘化民、項德禎等遮錫爵於朝房，面爭之。

translations.literal: Before long remonstrators grew more numerous, and Yue Yuansheng, Gu Yuncheng, Zhang Nalu, Chen Tailai, Yu Kongjian, Li Qimei, Zeng Fengyi, Zhong Huamin, Xiang Dezhen, and others blocked Xijue in the court anteroom and argued face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yue Yuansheng, Gu Yuncheng, Zhang Nalu, Chen Tailai, Yu Kongjian, Li Qimei, Zeng Fengyi, Zhong Huamin, Xiang Dezhen, and others cornered Xijue in the anteroom and debated him to his face.

sentences.zh: 李騰芳亦上書錫爵。

translations.literal: Li Tengfang also sent Xijue a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tengfang also memorialized Xijue directly.

sentences.zh: 錫爵請下廷議，不許。

translations.literal: Xijue asked that the matter be debated at court; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue asked for a full court debate; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 請面對，不報。

translations.literal: He asked for a personal audience; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a personal audience; no answer.

sentences.zh: 乃自劾三誤，乞罷斥。

translations.literal: He then impeached himself for three errors and begged dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He then confessed three errors and begged to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝亦迫公議，追寢前命，命少俟二三年議行。

translations.literal: The emperor, pressed by public opinion, revoked the earlier order and commanded that the matter wait two or three years.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by opinion, the emperor revoked the order and said to wait two or three years.

sentences.zh: 錫爵旋請速決，且曰：「曩元子初生，業為頒詔肆赦，詔書稱『祗承宗社』，明以皇太子待之矣。

translations.literal: Xijue soon asked for a swift decision and said: "When the eldest son was first born, an amnesty edict was already issued calling it 'receiving the charge of the ancestral temple'—clearly he was treated as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue soon pressed for a decision: "When the eldest son was born, an amnesty edict already called him 'receiving the ancestral charge'—he was plainly treated as heir.

sentences.zh: 今復何疑而弗決哉？

translations.literal: What doubt remains that it should not be settled?
translations.idiomatic: Why should there still be any hesitation?

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: No reply came.

sentences.zh: 七月，彗星見，有詔修省。

translations.literal: In the seventh month a comet appeared and an edict ordered self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month a comet appeared and the emperor ordered repentance.

sentences.zh: 錫爵因請延見大臣。

translations.literal: Xijue therefore asked that grand ministers be summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue asked that senior ministers be received in audience.

sentences.zh: 又言：「彗漸近紫微，宜慎起居之節，寬左右之刑，寡嗜欲以防疾，散積聚以廣恩。

translations.literal: He also said: "The comet is drawing near the Purple Forbidden Enclosure; Your Majesty should be careful in daily regimen, lighten punishments on those about you, limit desires to guard against illness, and disperse hoarded wealth to extend grace."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "The comet nears the Purple Forbidden Enclosure; temper daily habits, lighten punishments, curb desires against illness, and spend hoarded wealth on grace."

sentences.zh: 」逾月，復言：「慧已入紫微，非區區用人行政所能消弭，惟建儲一事可以禳之。

translations.literal: After more than a month he said again: "The comet has entered the Purple Forbidden Enclosure; this cannot be dispelled by mere personnel or policy changes—only establishing the heir can avert it."
translations.idiomatic: A month later: "The comet has entered the enclosure; only investiture of the heir can avert this—not routine appointments."

sentences.zh: 蓋天王之象曰帝星，太子之象曰前星。

translations.literal: For the sign of the Son of Heaven is the Imperial Star, and the heir's sign is the Front Star.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's star is the Imperial Star; the heir's is the Front Star.

sentences.zh: 今前星既耀而不早定，故致此災。

translations.literal: Now the Front Star shines yet no early decision is made—hence this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The Front Star shines yet no decision is made—hence this omen.

sentences.zh: 誠速行冊立，天變自弭。

translations.literal: If investiture is carried out swiftly, the heavenly warning will cease of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Investiture at once will still the heavens."

sentences.zh: 」帝皆報聞，仍持首春待期之說。

translations.literal: The emperor acknowledged receipt of all but still held to waiting until the coming spring.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted receipt but still insisted on waiting until spring.

sentences.zh: 錫爵答奏復力言之，又連章懇請。

translations.literal: Xijue replied and again spoke forcefully, submitting successive earnest memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue answered forcefully and memorialized again and again.

sentences.zh: 十一月，皇太后生辰，帝御門受賀畢，獨召錫爵暖閣，勞之曰：「卿扶母來京，誠忠孝兩全。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the empress dowager's birthday, after the emperor received congratulations at court he alone summoned Xijue to the warm pavilion and said in encouragement: "You brought your mother to the capital—truly filial piety and loyalty together."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, after the empress dowager's birthday audience, the emperor summoned Xijue alone to the warm pavilion: "You brought your mother to court—loyalty and filial piety together."

sentences.zh: 」錫爵叩頭謝，因力請早定國本。

translations.literal: Xijue kowtowed in thanks and forcefully asked that the foundation of the state be settled early.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue kowtowed and begged again to settle the succession.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「中宮有出，奈何？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If the empress has a son, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "But if the empress bears a son?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此說在十年前猶可，今元子已十三，尚何待？

translations.literal: He replied: "That argument might have worked ten years ago; the eldest son is already thirteen—what is there to wait for?"
translations.idiomatic: Xijue replied: "That might have worked ten years ago; the eldest son is thirteen—why wait?"

sentences.zh: 況自古至今，豈有子弟十三歲猶不讀書者？

translations.literal: Moreover, from antiquity to the present, has there ever been a youth of thirteen who still did not study?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, has any prince of thirteen ever gone without schooling?"

sentences.zh: 」帝頗感動。

translations.literal: The emperor was somewhat moved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved.

sentences.zh: 錫爵因請頻召對，保聖躬。

translations.literal: Xijue therefore asked for frequent audiences to safeguard the sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue asked for frequent audiences to protect the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 退復上疏力請，且曰：「外廷以固寵陰謀歸之皇貴妃，恐鄭氏舉族不得安。

translations.literal: On retiring he again memorialized forcefully, saying: "Outside the palace, people ascribe a secret plot to secure favor to the honored consort; I fear the Zheng clan will never know peace."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "Outside, they blame the honored consort for scheming to keep favor; I fear the Zheng family will never be safe.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下深省。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty reflect deeply."
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty reflect deeply."

sentences.zh: 」帝得疏，心益動，手詔諭錫爵：「卿每奏必及皇貴妃，何也？

translations.literal: When the emperor received the memorial he was moved still more and wrote in his own hand to Xijue: "Why does every memorial of yours mention the honored consort?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, stirred, wrote by hand: "Why does every memorial mention the honored consort?"

sentences.zh: 彼數勸朕，朕以祖訓後妃不得與外事，安敢輒從。

translations.literal: She has often urged me, but the ancestral injunction forbids consorts from outside affairs—how dare I lightly follow her."
translations.idiomatic: She often urges me, but ancestral rules bar consorts from outside affairs—how dare I obey?"

sentences.zh: 」錫爵上言：「今與皇長子相形者，惟皇貴妃子，天下不疑皇貴妃而誰疑？

translations.literal: Xijue submitted: "Today the only one who can be set against the eldest imperial son is the son of the honored consort—if the realm does not doubt the honored consort, whom does it doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: Xijue wrote: "Today only the honored consort's son stands against the eldest prince—if the realm does not doubt her, whom does it doubt?"

sentences.zh: 皇貴妃不引為己責而誰責？

translations.literal: If the honored consort does not take this as her own responsibility, whose is it?"
translations.idiomatic: If she does not accept responsibility, whose is it?"

sentences.zh: 祖訓不與外事者，不與外廷用人行政之事也。

translations.literal: The ancestral injunction against outside affairs means not interfering in appointments and administration outside the palace."
translations.idiomatic: That injunction means not meddling in outside appointments and policy—not family matters."

sentences.zh: 若冊立，乃陛下家事，而皇三子又皇貴妃親子，陛下得不與皇貴妃謀乎？

translations.literal: Investiture is Your Majesty's household affair, and the third imperial son is the honored consort's own child—must Your Majesty not consult her?"
translations.idiomatic: Investiture is Your Majesty's household affair, and the third son is her own child—must you not consult her?"

sentences.zh: 且皇貴妃久侍聖躬，至親且賢，外廷紛紛，莫不歸怨，臣所不忍聞。

translations.literal: Moreover the honored consort has long attended Your Majesty—most intimate and worthy; the clamor outside all turns to blame—I cannot bear to hear it."
translations.idiomatic: She has long served you—closest and worthy; outside blame I cannot bear to hear."

sentences.zh: 臣六十老人，力捍天下之口，歸功皇貴妃，陛下尚以為疑。

translations.literal: I am an old man of sixty who deflects the world's mouths to the honored consort's credit, yet Your Majesty still doubts."
translations.idiomatic: I am sixty, turning every tongue to her credit, yet you still doubt."

sentences.zh: 然則必如群少年盛氣以攻皇貴妃，而陛下反快於心乎？

translations.literal: Must it be that only when hot-blooded youths attack the honored consort in a body will Your Majesty feel satisfaction at heart?"
translations.idiomatic: Must hot-blooded youths attack her before you are satisfied?"

sentences.zh: 」疏入，帝頷之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in; the emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 誌臯、位亦力請。

translations.literal: Zhigao and Wei also pressed urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao and Wei pressed as well.

sentences.zh: 居數日，遂有出閣之命。

translations.literal: Within a few days there came the order to bring the heir out of the palace for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Within days came orders to bring the heir out for schooling.

sentences.zh: 而帝令廣市珠玉珍寶，供出閣儀物，計直三十余萬。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor ordered a broad purchase of pearls, jade, and treasures for the ceremony of leaving the palace, costing more than three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered pearls and jewels for the ceremony—over three hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書楊俊民等以故事爭，給事中王德完等又力諫。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Yang Junmin and others contested this by precedent; supervising secretaries Wang Dewan and others remonstrated forcefully as well.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yang Junmin cited precedent; supervising secretaries Wang Dewan and others remonstrated fiercely.

sentences.zh: 帝遂手詔諭爵，欲易期。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent a personal edict to Xijue wishing to change the date.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a handwritten note to Xijue wanting to change the date.

sentences.zh: 錫爵婉請，乃不果易。

translations.literal: Xijue tactfully asked, and the change did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue pleaded tactfully and the date held.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，出閣禮成，俱如東宮儀，中外為慰。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year the ceremony of leaving the palace was completed, all according to Eastern Palace rites; inside and outside the court were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The next second month the ceremony was completed per Eastern Palace rites; court and country breathed easier.

sentences.zh: 錫爵在閣時，嘗請罷江南織造，停江西陶器，減雲南貢金，出內帑振河南饑，帝皆無忤，眷禮逾前後諸輔臣。

translations.literal: While Xijue was in the Grand Secretariat he asked to end Jiangnan textile manufacture, halt Jiangxi pottery, reduce Yunnan tribute gold, and release inner-palace funds to relieve famine in Henan; the emperor raised no objection, and his favor exceeded that shown earlier Grand Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: In office he sought to end Jiangnan silk workshops, halt Jiangxi pottery, cut Yunnan gold tribute, and release palace funds for Henan famine—all accepted; favor exceeded any earlier chief minister.

sentences.zh: 其救李沂，力爭不宜用廷杖，尤為世所稱。

translations.literal: His rescue of Li Yi and his forceful argument that court beating should not be used were especially praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His defense of Li Yi and his stand against court flogging won special praise.

sentences.zh: 特以阿並封指被物議。

translations.literal: Only because he went along with simultaneous enfeoffment did he suffer public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Only his acquiescence in simultaneous enfeoffment drew public blame.

sentences.zh: 既而郎中趙南星斥，侍郎趙用賢放歸，論救者咸遭譴謫，眾指錫爵為之。

translations.literal: Later Director Zhao Nanxing was dismissed and Vice Minister Zhao Yongxian sent home; those who pleaded for them were all punished and demoted—the multitude pointed at Xijue as the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao Nanxing was dismissed and Zhao Yongxian sent home; defenders were punished—all blamed Xijue.

sentences.zh: 雖連章自明，且申救，人卒莫能諒也。

translations.literal: Though he repeatedly clarified himself in memorials and also pleaded for them, people could never quite forgive him.
translations.idiomatic: Though he explained himself and pleaded for them, he was never fully forgiven.

sentences.zh: 錫爵遂屢疏引疾乞休。

translations.literal: Xijue therefore submitted successive memorials citing illness and asking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue repeatedly begged to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 帝不欲其去，為出內帑錢建醮祈愈。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish him to go and spent inner-palace funds on rituals praying for his recovery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to let him go and spent palace funds on rituals for his recovery.

sentences.zh: 錫爵力辭，疏八上乃允。

translations.literal: Xijue strove to decline forcefully; only after eight memorials was consent granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue declined repeatedly; only after eight memorials was he allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 先累加太子太保，至是命改吏部尚書，進建極殿，賜道里費，乘傳，行人護歸。

translations.literal: He had earlier been cumulatively promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; now he was ordered to change to Minister of Personnel, advanced to the Jianji Hall, granted traveling expenses, given post-horses, and escorted home by an imperial messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Previously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, he was now named Minister of Personnel, advanced to Jianji Hall, given traveling funds and post-horses, and escorted home by an imperial messenger.

sentences.zh: 歸七年，東宮建，遣官賜敕存問，賚銀幣羊酒。

translations.literal: Seven years after his return, when the Eastern Palace was established, officials were sent with an imperial letter of inquiry and gifts of silver, silk coins, sheep, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later, when the crown prince's residence was built, the court sent officials with an imperial message and gifts of silver, silk, sheep, and wine.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，廷推閣臣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, Grand Secretaries were recommended at court.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-five, the court recommended candidates for the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝既用於慎行、葉向高、李廷機，還念錫爵，特加少保，遺官召之。

translations.literal: The emperor had already appointed Yu Shenxing, Ye Xianggao, and Li Tingji, yet still thought of Xijue and specially added him as Junior Guardian, sending an official to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Having appointed Yu Shenxing, Ye Xianggao, and Li Tingji, the emperor still recalled Xijue, made him Junior Guardian, and sent to summon him.

sentences.zh: 三辭，不允。

translations.literal: He declined three times; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined three times but was refused.

sentences.zh: 時言官方厲鋒氣，錫爵進密揭力詆，中有「上於章奏一概留中，特鄙夷之如禽鳥之音」等語。

translations.literal: At the time censorial officials were said to be fierce in spirit; Xijue submitted a secret memorial forcefully denouncing them, including the words: 'Your Majesty keeps all memorials undecided and especially despises them like the sounds of birds.'
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials were riding high; Xijue sent a secret memorial attacking them, saying the emperor held all memorials in abeyance and scorned remonstrators like bird calls.

sentences.zh: 言官聞之大憤。

translations.literal: The censorial officials heard this and were greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The censorial officials were furious when they learned of it.

sentences.zh: 給事中段然首劾之，其同官胡嘉棟等論不已。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Duan Ran was first to impeach him; his colleagues Hu Jiadong and others debated without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ran led the impeachment; Hu Jiadong and fellow supervising secretaries kept up the attack.

sentences.zh: 錫爵亦自闔門養重，竟辭不赴。

translations.literal: Xijue also shut his gates to cultivate his standing and in the end declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue shut his gates and in the end refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 又三年，卒於家，年七十七。

translations.literal: Three years later he died at home, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died at home at seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚文肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 子 衡

translations.literal: Son: Heng
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng

sentences.zh: 子衡，字辰玉，少有文名。

translations.literal: His son Heng, style name Chenyu, had a literary reputation from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng, styled Chenyu, was known for letters from youth.

sentences.zh: 為舉首才，自稱因被論，遂不復會試。

translations.literal: As top talent in the provincial examination, he said that because he had been criticized he would no longer take the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Top of the provincial rolls, he claimed that after being criticized he would not sit for the metropolitan exam again.

sentences.zh: 至二十九年，錫爵罷相已久，始舉會試第二人，廷試亦第二。

translations.literal: Only in the twenty-ninth year, long after Xijue had left the premiership, did he take the metropolitan examination as second place and the palace examination also as second.
translations.idiomatic: Not until year twenty-nine, long after his father left office, did he place second in both the metropolitan and palace examinations.

sentences.zh: 授編修，先父卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Compiler; his father died first.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Compiler, he was preceded in death by his father.

sentences.zh: 弟 鼎爵

translations.literal: Younger brother: Dingjue
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Dingjue

sentences.zh: 錫爵弟鼎爵，進士。

translations.literal: Xijue's younger brother Dingjue was a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue's younger brother Dingjue passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 累官河南提學副使。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Vice Commissioner of Education in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Commissioner of Education in Henan.

sentences.zh: 沈一貫

translations.literal: Shen Yiguan
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yiguan

sentences.zh: 沈一貫，字肩吾，鄞人。

translations.literal: Shen Yiguan, style name Jianwu, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yiguan, styled Jianwu, was from Yin.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Longqing year two.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授檢討，充日講官。

translations.literal: Selected as Hanlin Bachelor, appointed Reviser, and made a Daily Lecture official.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as Hanlin Bachelor, made Reviser and Daily Lecture official.

sentences.zh: 進講高宗諒陰，拱手曰：「托孤寄命，必忠貞不二心之臣，乃可使百官總己以聽。

translations.literal: Advancing to lecture on Gaozong's mourning seclusion, he clasped his hands and said: 'Entrusting an orphan and committing the mandate require a loyal minister of undivided heart before one may have the hundred officials gather affairs and listen to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturing on Gaozong's mourning seclusion, he said: 'Entrusting an orphan requires a loyal minister of undivided heart before officials may gather affairs and obey.

sentences.zh: 茍非其人，不若躬親聽覽之為孝也。

translations.literal: If it is not such a person, personally attending to affairs and listening is the greater filial piety.'
translations.idiomatic: If not such a man, personally hearing affairs is the greater filial piety.'

sentences.zh: 」張居正以為刺己，頗憾一貫。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng took this as aimed at himself and resented Yiguan considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng took this as a barb at himself and bore considerable resentment toward Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 居正卒，始遷左中允。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, he was first promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歷官吏部左侍郎兼侍讀學士，加太子賓客。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister of Personnel on the left and Reader-in-Waiting, and was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister of Personnel and Reader-in-Waiting, then Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 假歸。

translations.literal: He took leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 二十二年起南京禮部尚書，復召為正史副總裁，協理詹事府，未上。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was made Minister of Rites at Nanjing, then recalled as Deputy Chief Compiler of the Veritable Records, to assist in the Household of the Heir Apparent, but had not reported when—
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two he was made Nanjing Minister of Rites, then recalled as Deputy Chief Compiler and to assist the Heir Apparent's household, but had not reported when—

sentences.zh: 王錫爵、趙誌臯、張位同居內閣，復有旨推舉閣臣。

translations.literal: Wang Xijue, Zhao Zhigao, and Zhang Wei were together in the Grand Secretariat, and there was again an edict recommending Grand Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue, Zhigao, and Wei were in the Grand Secretariat when another edict called for new Grand Secretaries.

sentences.zh: 吏部舉舊輔王家屏及一貫等七人名以上。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel submitted the names of seven men including former Grand Secretary Wang Jiaping and Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel submitted seven names including Wang Jiaping and Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 而帝方怒家屏，譙責尚書陳有年。

translations.literal: But the emperor was then angry at Jiaping and rebuked Minister Chen Younian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry at Jiaping and rebuked Minister Chen Younian.

sentences.zh: 有年引疾去。

translations.literal: Younian cited illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Younian resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 一貫家居久，故有清望，閣臣又力薦之。

translations.literal: Yiguan had long lived at home and therefore had a clean reputation; the Grand Secretaries also strongly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Long at home, Yiguan enjoyed a clean reputation; the Grand Secretaries strongly backed him.

sentences.zh: 乃詔以尚書兼東閣大學士，與陳於陛同入閣預機務，命行人即家起焉。

translations.literal: An edict then named him Minister and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, to enter the Grand Secretariat with Chen Yubi to handle state affairs; an imperial messenger was sent to summon him from his home.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Minister and Eastern Pavilion Grand Secretary, to enter the Grand Secretariat with Chen Yubi; a messenger was sent to fetch him from home.

sentences.zh: 會朝議許日本封貢。

translations.literal: At the time the court was debating permitting Japanese tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then debating Japanese tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 一貫慮貢道出寧波，為鄉郡患，極陳其害，貢議乃止。

translations.literal: Yiguan feared the tribute route would pass through Ningbo and harm his home region; he set forth the harm at length, and the tribute proposal was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the tribute route through Ningbo would harm his home region, Yiguan argued at length and the tribute plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 未幾，錫爵去，於陛位第三，每獨行己意。

translations.literal: Before long Xijue left; Yubi ranked third and often acted on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xijue left; Yubi ranked third and often went his own way.

sentences.zh: 一貫柔而深中，事誌臯等惟謹。

translations.literal: Yiguan was soft yet inwardly calculating; in dealing with Zhigao and the others he was only cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan was outwardly mild but inwardly deep; toward Zhigao and others he was meticulously deferential.

sentences.zh: 其後於陛卒官，誌臯病痹久在告，位以薦楊鎬及《憂危竑議》事得罪去，一貫與位嘗私致鎬書，為贊畫主事丁應泰所劾。

translations.literal: Later Yubi died in office; Zhigao long suffered paralysis and was on leave; Wei left office disgraced over recommending Yang Hao and the Youwei Jingyi affair; Yiguan and Wei had once privately sent letters to Hao and were impeached by Director Ding Yingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yubi died in office; Zhigao was long ill on leave; Wei fell over Yang Hao and the Youwei Jingyi affair; Yiguan and Wei had privately written Hao and were impeached by Ding Yingtai.

sentences.zh: 位疏辨，激上怒罷。

translations.literal: Wei memorialized in defense, provoking the emperor's anger and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's defense memorial provoked the emperor's wrath and his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 一貫惟引咎，帝乃慰留之。

translations.literal: Yiguan only cited guilt; the emperor then comforted him and kept him.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan took only blame upon himself; the emperor comforted him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 時國本未定，廷臣爭十餘年不決。

translations.literal: At the time the succession was unsettled; court officials disputed it for more than ten years without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent was unsettled; the court debated it over ten years without resolution.

sentences.zh: 皇長子年十八，諸請冊立冠婚者益迫。

translations.literal: The eldest imperial son was eighteen; those requesting investiture, capping, and marriage pressed all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son was eighteen; pleas for investiture, capping, and marriage grew urgent.

sentences.zh: 帝責戶部進銀二千四百萬，為冊立、分封諸典禮費以困之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Ministry of Revenue to advance twenty-four million taels of silver as costs for investiture, enfeoffment, and other ritual expenses to thwart them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demanded twenty-four million taels from Revenue for investiture and enfeoffment costs to thwart the pleas.

sentences.zh: 一貫再疏爭，不聽。

translations.literal: Yiguan memorialized twice in protest; he was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan protested twice in memorials but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，命營慈慶宮居皇長子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he ordered the Ciqing Palace built to house the eldest imperial son.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight he ordered the Ciqing Palace built for the eldest son.

sentences.zh: 工竣，諭一貫草敕傳示禮官，上冊立、冠婚及諸王分封儀。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he instructed Yiguan to draft an edict for transmission to the ritual officials, setting forth rites for investiture, capping and marriage, and enfeoffment of the princes.
translations.idiomatic: When construction finished, he had Yiguan draft an edict for ritual officials on investiture, capping, marriage, and princely enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 敕既上，帝復留不下。

translations.literal: After the edict was submitted, the emperor again kept it undecided.
translations.idiomatic: After submission the emperor again withheld the edict.

sentences.zh: 一貫疏趣，則言：「朕因小臣謝廷讃乘機邀功，故中輟。

translations.literal: Yiguan memorialized to press it; then he said: 'Because petty officials such as Xie Tingzan seized the moment to seek merit, I therefore halted it midway.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan pressed for promulgation; the emperor replied that petty officials like Xie Tingzan had seized merit, so he halted it midway.

sentences.zh: 俟皇長子移居後行之。

translations.literal: Wait until after the eldest imperial son moves in, then carry it out.'
translations.idiomatic: It would be carried out after the eldest son moved in.'

sentences.zh: 」既而不舉行。

translations.literal: Afterward it was still not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward it was still not carried out.

sentences.zh: 明年，貴妃弟鄭國泰迫群議，請冊立、冠婚並行。

translations.literal: The next year, the favored consort's brother Zheng Guotai, pressed by public debate, requested investiture and capping and marriage together.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the consort's brother Zheng Guotai, under public pressure, asked for investiture and capping and marriage together.

sentences.zh: 一貫因再草敕請下禮官具儀，不報。

translations.literal: Yiguan therefore again drafted an edict asking that it be sent down for ritual officials to prepare the rites; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan again drafted an edict for ritual officials to prepare rites; there was no response.

sentences.zh: 廷議有欲先冠婚後冊立者，一貫不可，曰：「不正名而茍成事，是降儲君為諸王也。

translations.literal: In court debate some wished to cap and marry first and invest later; Yiguan would not allow it, saying: 'To accomplish the affair without rectifying the name is to reduce the heir to the rank of ordinary princes.'
translations.idiomatic: Some in court wanted capping and marriage before investiture; Yiguan refused, saying that without rectifying the name one reduced the heir to an ordinary prince.

sentences.zh: 」會帝意亦頗悟，命即日舉行。

translations.literal: When the emperor's mind also came partly to understand, he ordered it carried out that very day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came partly to his senses and ordered it carried out that day.

sentences.zh: 九月十有八日漏下二鼓，詔下。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the ninth month, at the second watch after midnight, the edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth of the ninth month, at the second watch past midnight, the edict came down.

sentences.zh: 既而帝復悔，令改期。

translations.literal: Soon after the emperor again regretted it and ordered the date changed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor regretted it and ordered the date changed.

sentences.zh: 一貫封還詔書，言「萬死不敢奉詔」，帝乃止。

translations.literal: Yiguan returned the sealed edict, saying 'I dare not obey on pain of ten thousand deaths'; the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan returned the edict, saying he dared not obey on pain of death; the emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 十月望，冊立禮成，時論頗稱之。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth of the tenth month the investiture rites were completed; public opinion praised him considerably.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the tenth month investiture was completed; opinion praised Yiguan highly.

sentences.zh: 會誌臯於九月卒，一貫遂當國。

translations.literal: When Zhigao died in the ninth month, Yiguan then held the government.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigao died in the ninth month, Yiguan came to head the government.

sentences.zh: 初，誌臯病久，一貫屢請增閣臣。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Zhigao had long been ill, Yiguan repeatedly asked to add Grand Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhigao had long been ill, Yiguan had repeatedly asked to add Grand Secretaries.

sentences.zh: 及是乃簡用沈鯉、朱賡，而事皆取決於一貫。

translations.literal: Only now were Shen Li and Zhu Geng selected, yet affairs were all decided by Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shen Li and Zhu Geng were selected, but Yiguan decided everything.

sentences.zh: 尋進太子太保、戶部尚書、武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand Guardian, Minister of Revenue, and Wuying Hall Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 自一貫入內閣，朝政已大非。

translations.literal: From the time Yiguan entered the Grand Secretariat, court government was already greatly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yiguan entered the Grand Secretariat, court government had already gone badly wrong.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，礦稅使四出為民害。

translations.literal: Within a few years, mining-tax envoys went out on all sides and became a scourge to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years mining-tax envoys spread everywhere and harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 其所誣劾逮系者，悉滯獄中。

translations.literal: Those falsely impeached and arrested were all held long in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Those falsely impeached and imprisoned all languished in jail.

sentences.zh: 吏部疏請起用建言廢黜諸臣，並考選科道官，久抑不下，中外多以望閣臣。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel memorialized asking to recall dismissed remonstrating officials and to examine and select censorial officials; it was long suppressed undecided, and inside and outside the court mostly looked to the Grand Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel asked to recall dismissed remonstrators and fill censorial posts; the memorial was long withheld, and court and country looked to the Grand Secretaries.

sentences.zh: 一貫等數諫，不省。

translations.literal: Yiguan and the others remonstrated several times; the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan and others remonstrated repeatedly without effect.

sentences.zh: 而帝久不視朝，閣臣屢請，皆不報。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor long did not attend court; the Grand Secretaries repeatedly asked and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor long skipped court; Grand Secretaries' repeated requests went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 一貫初輔政面恩，一見帝而已。

translations.literal: When Yiguan first assisted in government he was granted an imperial audience; he saw the emperor only that once.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiguan first took office he was granted one audience; he never saw the emperor again.

sentences.zh: 東征及楊應龍平，帝再御午門樓受俘。

translations.literal: On the eastern campaign and when Yang Yinglong was pacified, the emperor twice took the noon gate tower to receive captives.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern campaign and Yang Yinglong's defeat, the emperor twice received captives at the Meridian Gate.

sentences.zh: 一貫請陪侍，賜面對，皆不許。

translations.literal: Yiguan asked to attend in support and requested a face audience; both were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan asked to attend and for an audience; both were refused.

sentences.zh: 上下否隔甚，一貫雖小有救正，大率依違其間，物望漸減。

translations.literal: The gap between above and below was very great; though Yiguan made small corrections here and there, for the most part he wavered between them, and public esteem gradually declined.
