translations.idiomatic: Emperor and ministers were deeply estranged; Yiguan made small fixes but mostly wavered, and his standing faded.

sentences.zh: 迨三十年二月，皇太子婚禮甫成，帝忽有疾。

translations.literal: By the second month of the thirtieth year, when the crown prince's wedding had just been completed, the emperor suddenly fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year thirty, right after the crown prince's wedding, the emperor fell suddenly ill.

sentences.zh: 急召諸大臣至仁德門，俄獨命一貫入啟祥宮後殿暖西閣。

translations.literal: He urgently summoned the great ministers to the Rende Gate; presently he alone ordered Yiguan into the warm western chamber behind the rear hall of the Qixiang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned ministers to Rende Gate, then ordered Yiguan alone into the warm western chamber behind Qixiang Palace.

sentences.zh: 皇后、貴妃以疾不侍側，皇太后南面立稍北，帝稍東，冠服席地坐，亦南面，太子、諸王跪於前。

translations.literal: The empress and favored consort did not attend at his side because of illness; the empress dowager stood facing south slightly to the north, the emperor slightly east; crown and robes, seated on the ground, also facing south; the crown prince and princes knelt before him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress and consort could not attend owing to illness; the empress dowager stood facing south, the emperor east in crown and robes seated on the ground; the crown prince and princes knelt before them.

sentences.zh: 一貫叩頭起居訖，帝曰：「先生前。

translations.literal: After Yiguan kowtowed and inquired after his health, the emperor said: 'Sir, come forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan kowtowed and inquired; the emperor said: 'Sir, come forward.

sentences.zh: 朕病日篤矣，享國已久，何憾。

translations.literal: My illness grows daily worse; I have enjoyed the realm long—what regret is there?
translations.idiomatic: My illness grows worse daily; I have reigned long—what regret is there?

sentences.zh: 佳兒佳婦付與先生，惟輔之為賢君。

translations.literal: I entrust my fine son and fine daughter-in-law to you, sir; only assist him to become a worthy ruler.'
translations.idiomatic: I entrust my fine son and daughter-in-law to you; only help him become a worthy ruler.'

sentences.zh: 礦稅事，朕因殿工未竣，權宜采取，今可與江南織造、江西陶器俱止勿行，所遣內監皆令還京。

translations.literal: As for mining taxes, because palace construction was not yet finished I took them as a temporary measure; now stop them together with Jiangnan weaving and Jiangxi pottery; send all the eunuchs dispatched back to the capital.'
translations.idiomatic: Mining taxes I took temporarily while palace works were unfinished; now stop them with Jiangnan weaving and Jiangxi pottery and recall all dispatched eunuchs.'

sentences.zh: 法司釋久系罪囚，建言得罪諸臣咸復其官，給事中、御史即如所請補用。

translations.literal: The judicial offices should release long-imprisoned convicts; remonstrators punished for speaking should all have their offices restored; supervising secretaries and censors should be filled as requested.'
translations.idiomatic: Release long-held prisoners; restore remonstrators; fill supervising secretaries and censors as requested.'

sentences.zh: 朕見先生止此矣。

translations.literal: I shall see you, sir, only this once.'
translations.idiomatic: I shall see you only this once.'

sentences.zh: 」言已就臥。

translations.literal: When he had spoken he lay down.
translations.idiomatic: Having spoken, he lay down.

sentences.zh: 一貫哭，太后、太子、諸王皆哭。

translations.literal: Yiguan wept; the empress dowager, crown prince, and princes all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan wept; the empress dowager, crown prince, and princes wept.

sentences.zh: 一貫復奏：「今尚書求去者三，請定去留。

translations.literal: Yiguan again memorialized: 'Now three ministers ask to leave; please decide who goes and who stays.'
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan added: 'Three ministers seek to leave; please decide who stays.'

sentences.zh: 」帝留戶部陳渠、兵部田樂，而以祖陵沖決，削工部楊一魁籍。

translations.literal: The emperor kept Chen Qu of Revenue and Tian Le of War, but because the imperial tombs were damaged by flooding he stripped Yang Yikui of the Ministry of Works from the register.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept Chen Qu and Tian Le but stripped Works Minister Yang Yikui from the register over tomb flooding.

sentences.zh: 一貫復叩首，出擬旨以進。

translations.literal: Yiguan kowtowed again, went out, and drafted the rescript for submission.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan kowtowed again, withdrew, and drafted the rescript for submission.

sentences.zh: 是夕，閣臣九卿俱直宿朝房。

translations.literal: That evening, all Grand Secretaries and the Nine Ministers kept night watch in the court chambers.
translations.idiomatic: That night Grand Secretaries and the Nine Ministers kept watch in the court chambers.

sentences.zh: 漏三鼓，中使捧諭至，具如帝語一貫者。

translations.literal: At the third watch, palace messengers brought an edict down, fully matching what the emperor had told Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: At the third watch messengers brought an edict matching the emperor's words to Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣咸喜。

translations.literal: All the great ministers were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: All the great ministers rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 翼日，帝疾，廖悔之。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor fell ill and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when the emperor fell ill, he regretted it.

sentences.zh: 中使二十輩至閣中取前諭，言礦稅不可罷，釋囚、錄直臣惟卿所裁。

translations.literal: Twenty palace messengers came to the Grand Secretariat to fetch the earlier edict, saying mining taxes could not be stopped and that releasing prisoners and restoring upright officials were for Yiguan alone to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty messengers came to fetch the earlier edict, saying mining taxes could not stop and that prisoners and restored officials were for Yiguan to decide.

sentences.zh: 一貫欲不予，中使輒搏顙幾流血，一貫惶遽繳入。

translations.literal: Yiguan wished not to give it; the messengers beat their foreheads until nearly bleeding; Yiguan in panic handed it in.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan hesitated to surrender it; the messengers battered their foreheads nearly to bleeding until he handed it in in panic.

sentences.zh: 時吏部尚書李戴、左都御史溫純期即日奉行，頒示天下，刑部尚書蕭大亨則謂弛獄須再請。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Personnel Li Dai and Left Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun expected to carry it out that very day and proclaim it to the realm; Minister of Punishments Xiao Daheng said emptying the prisons required another request.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dai and Wen Chun expected immediate proclamation; Xiao Daheng said emptying prisons required another order.

sentences.zh: 無何，事變。

translations.literal: Before long the affair changed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long matters changed.

sentences.zh: 太仆卿南企仲劾戴、大亨不即奉帝諭，起廢釋囚。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Stud Nan Qizhong impeached Dai and Daheng for not immediately carrying out the emperor's edict to restore the dismissed and release prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Qizhong impeached Dai and Daheng for not immediately executing the edict to restore officials and release prisoners.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，並二事寢不行。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and both matters were shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and both measures were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 當帝欲追還成命，司禮太監田義力爭。

translations.literal: When the emperor wished to recall the completed edict, Director of Ceremonies eunuch Tian Yi argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the emperor wished to recall the edict he had already issued, the eunuch Tian Yi, Director of Ceremonies, argued against it with all his might.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲手刃之。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and wished to kill him with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and meant to kill him with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 義言愈力，而中使已持一貫所繳前諭至。

translations.literal: Yi spoke with ever greater force, but palace messengers had already arrived bearing the earlier edict Yiguan had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yi pressed his argument harder still, yet messengers had already arrived carrying the earlier edict Yiguan had handed in.

sentences.zh: 後義見一貫唾曰：「相公稍持之，礦稅撤矣，何怯也！

translations.literal: Later Yi saw Yiguan and spat, saying, "My lord, hold firm a little longer—the mining tax will be withdrawn; why so timid!
translations.idiomatic: Later Tian Yi saw Yiguan and spat at him: "Chancellor, hold your ground a little longer—the mining tax will be lifted. Why so faint-hearted!

sentences.zh: 」自是大臣言官疏請者日相繼，皆不復聽。

translations.literal: " From then on memorials from grand ministers and remonstrance officials requesting [reversal] came day after day in succession, but [the emperor] would no longer listen.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on ministers and censors submitted memorial after memorial asking the same, and the emperor would not hear them.

sentences.zh: 礦稅之害，遂終神宗世。

translations.literal: The harm of mining taxes thus lasted through Shenzong's entire reign.
translations.idiomatic: The scourge of mining taxes thus endured to the end of Shenzong's reign.

sentences.zh: 帝自疾瘳以後，政益廢弛。

translations.literal: After the emperor recovered from his illness, government grew ever more lax.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor recovered from his illness, government slackened still further.

sentences.zh: 稅監王朝、梁永、高淮等所至橫暴，奸人乘機虐民者愈眾。

translations.literal: Tax commissioners Wang Chao, Liang Yong, Gao Huai, and others were violent wherever they went, and scoundrels who seized the moment to abuse the people grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioners Wang Chao, Liang Yong, and Gao Huai ran riot wherever they went, and ever more villains took the chance to prey on the people.

sentences.zh: 一貫與鯉、賡共著論以風，又嘗因事屢爭，且揭陳用人行政諸事。

translations.literal: Yiguan together with Li and Geng jointly composed essays to admonish, and on several occasions disputed matters repeatedly, moreover laying out personnel and administration issues.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan, Li, and Geng wrote joint essays of admonition, quarreled with the throne over one matter after another, and repeatedly laid out how men were appointed and how policy was run.

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 顧遇一貫厚，嘗特賜敕獎之。

translations.literal: Yet his treatment of Yiguan was generous; he once specially bestowed an edict of commendation on him.
translations.idiomatic: Even so he favored Yiguan generously and once issued a special edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 一貫素忌鯉，鯉亦自以講筵受主眷，非由一貫進，不為下，二人漸不相能。

translations.literal: Yiguan had long resented Li; Li also considered that through the lecture hall he enjoyed the sovereign's favor, having not been advanced by Yiguan, and would not defer—gradually the two could not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan had long resented Li, and Li for his part knew the emperor cherished him for his lectures, not through Yiguan's patronage, and would not yield. Gradually the two could no longer work together.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎郭正域以文章氣節著，鯉甚重之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Guo Zhengyu was renowned for literary talent and integrity; Li greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Guo Zhengyu was known for his writing and moral backbone, and Li held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 都御史溫純、吏部侍郎楊時喬皆以清嚴自持相標置，一貫不善也。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun and Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Shiqiao both held themselves to strict purity and marked themselves off as such; Yiguan disliked them.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun and Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Shiqiao both prided themselves on stern rectitude; Yiguan disliked them.

sentences.zh: 會正域議奪呂本謚，一貫、賡與本同鄉，寢其議。

translations.literal: When Zhengyu proposed stripping Lu Ben of his posthumous title, Yiguan and Geng were fellow-townsmen of Ben's and shelved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengyu moved to strip Lu Ben of his posthumous title, Yiguan and Geng, who shared Ben's home district, buried the proposal.

sentences.zh: 由是益惡正域，並惡鯉及純、時喬等，而黨論漸興。

translations.literal: Thereupon he hated Zhengyu the more, and likewise hated Li and Chun, Shiqiao, and others, and factional rhetoric gradually arose.
translations.idiomatic: He hated Zhengyu all the more, and with him Li, Chun, Shiqiao, and the rest; factional strife began to stir.

sentences.zh: 浙人與公論忤，由一貫始。

translations.literal: The clash between men of Zhejiang and public opinion began with Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: The rift between Zhejiang men and the moral consensus of the court began with Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，楚府鎮國將軍華勣訐楚王華奎為假王。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, Defender-in-Chief of the Chu princely establishment Hua Ji impeached Prince of Chu Hua Kui as a false prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of Wanli, Defender-in-Chief Hua Ji of the Chu princely house accused Prince Hua Kui of being an impostor.

sentences.zh: 一貫納王重賄，令通政司格其疏月余，先上華奎劾華勣欺罔四罪疏。

translations.literal: Yiguan accepted heavy bribes from the prince, had the Transmission Office hold Ji's memorial for more than a month, and first forwarded Kui's four-charge memorial impeaching Ji for deception.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan took heavy bribes from the prince, had the Transmission Office sit on Ji's memorial for more than a month, and first forwarded Kui's memorial charging Ji with four counts of fraud.

sentences.zh: 正域，楚人，頗聞假王事有狀，請行勘虛實以定罪案。

translations.literal: Zhengyu, a man of Chu, had heard considerable evidence in the false-prince affair and requested an investigation to determine guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu, himself a man of Chu, had heard strong evidence in the impostor case and asked for a formal inquiry before fixing guilt.

sentences.zh: 一貫持之。

translations.literal: Yiguan held firm against it.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan blocked him.

sentences.zh: 正域以楚王饋遺書上，帝不省。

translations.literal: Zhengyu submitted a letter on gifts from the Prince of Chu; the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu memorialized about gifts from the Prince of Chu; the emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 及撫按臣會勘並廷臣集議疏入，一貫力右王，嗾給事中錢夢臯、楊應文劾正域，勒歸聽勘，華勣等皆得罪。

translations.literal: When the provincial governor and censor's joint investigation and the court officials' collective deliberation memorials arrived, Yiguan strongly backed the prince, instigating supervising secretaries Qian Menggao and Yang Yingwen to impeach Zhengyu, compelling him to return home pending investigation; Ji and others were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the joint report of the provincial officials and the court's collective deliberation reached the throne, Yiguan threw his weight behind the prince, set Menggao and Yingwen to impeach Zhengyu, forced him home to await judgment, and punished Ji and his allies.

sentences.zh: 正域甫登舟，未行，而「妖書」事起。

translations.literal: Zhengyu had just boarded his boat and not yet departed when the "demon book" affair arose.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyu had just stepped aboard his boat and not yet cast off when the Demon Book affair broke out.

sentences.zh: 一貫方銜正域與鯉，其黨康丕揚、錢夢臯等遂捕僧達觀、醫生沈令譽等下獄，窮治之。

translations.literal: Yiguan was just then bearing grudges against Zhengyu and Li; his partisans Kang Piyang, Qian Menggao, and others thereupon arrested the monk Daguan, the physician Shen Lingyu, and others and put them in prison, investigating to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan still nursed his grudge against Zhengyu and Li; his men Kang Piyang, Menggao, and the rest arrested the monk Daguan, the physician Shen Lingyu, and others and tortured the case to its limit.

sentences.zh: 一貫從中主其事，令錦衣帥王之禎與丕揚大索鯉私第三日，發卒圍正域舟，執掠其婢仆乳媼，皆無所得。

translations.literal: Yiguan directed matters from behind, ordering Commander of the Brocade Guard Wang Zhizhen and Piyang to search Li's private residence on a large scale for three days, and sent troops to surround Zhengyu's boat and seize and search his maidservants, attendants, and wet nurses—all to no avail.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan ran the affair from behind the scenes, sent Wang Zhizhen of the Brocade Guard and Piyang to ransack Li's private residence for three days, and sent soldiers to surround Zhengyu's boat and seize his maids, servants, and wet nurses—yet found nothing.

sentences.zh: 乃以生光具獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon they fabricated a full case against Kuang Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they pinned the crime on Kuang Guang and closed the case.

sentences.zh: 二事錯見正域及楚王傳中。

translations.literal: The two affairs are treated in scattered passages in the biographies of Zhengyu and the Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Both affairs are recounted in the biographies of Zhengyu and the Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 始，都御史純劾御史於永清及給事中姚文蔚，語稍涉一貫。

translations.literal: At first, Censor-in-Chief Chun impeached censor Yu Yongqing and supervising secretary Yao Wenwei, the wording somewhat touching Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun had impeached censor Yu Yongqing and supervising secretary Yao Wenwei in terms that touched Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 給事中鐘兆鬥為一貫論純，御史湯兆京復劾兆鬥而直純。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zhong Zhaodou argued on Yiguan's behalf against Chun; censor Tang Zhaojing again impeached Zhaodou and upheld Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhong Zhaodou spoke up for Yiguan against Chun; censor Tang Zhaojing impeached Zhaodou in turn and took Chun's side.

sentences.zh: 純十七疏求去，一貫佯揭留純。

translations.literal: Chun submitted seventeen memorials requesting departure; Yiguan pretended to post a notice retaining Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Chun memorialized seventeen times to resign; Yiguan pretended to post a public notice urging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 至歲乙巳，大察京朝官。

translations.literal: When the yisi year came, the great evaluation of capital officials was held.
translations.idiomatic: In the yisi year came the great evaluation of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 純與時喬主其事，夢臯、兆鬥皆在黜中。

translations.literal: Chun and Shiqiao presided over it; Menggao and Zhaodou were both among those marked for dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and Shiqiao ran it; Menggao and Zhaodou were both on the dismissal list.

sentences.zh: 一貫怒，言於帝，以京察疏留。

translations.literal: Yiguan was angry, spoke to the emperor, and had the capital-evaluation memorial held back.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan was furious, spoke to the emperor, and had the evaluation memorial held in the palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃盡留給事、御史之被察者，且許純致仕去。

translations.literal: After a long time, all supervising secretaries and censors who had been evaluated were retained, and Chun was permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long delay were all the evaluated supervising secretaries and censors kept in post, while Chun was allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 於是主事劉元珍、龐時雍、南京御史朱吾弼力爭之，謂二百余年計典無特留者。

translations.literal: Thereupon section chief Liu Yuanzhen, Pang Shiyong, and Nanjing censor Zhu Wubi argued forcefully, saying that in more than two hundred years of the evaluation cycle there had never been a special retention.
translations.idiomatic: Section chiefs Liu Yuanzhen and Pang Shiyong and Nanjing censor Zhu Wubi protested fiercely that in more than two hundred years of evaluations no one had ever been specially retained.

sentences.zh: 時南察疏亦留中，後迫眾議始下。

translations.literal: At the time the southern evaluation memorial was also held in the palace; only later, pressed by public opinion, was it issued.
translations.idiomatic: The southern evaluation memorial was held back as well and was issued only when public pressure mounted.

sentences.zh: 一貫自是積不為公論所與，彈劾日眾，因謝病不出。

translations.literal: From then on Yiguan accumulated ever less support from public opinion, impeachments grew daily, and he pleaded illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: After that Yiguan lost the court's respect day by day, impeachments piled up, and he pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 三十上四年七月，給事中陳嘉訓、御史孫居相復連章劾其奸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, seventh month, supervising secretary Chen Jiaxun and censor Sun Juxiang again submitted linked memorials impeaching his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the thirty-fourth year, supervising secretary Chen Jiaxun and censor Sun Juxiang again filed joint memorials denouncing his corruption.

sentences.zh: 一貫憤，益求去。

translations.literal: Yiguan was indignant and sought departure all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan, furious, pressed all the harder to leave office.

sentences.zh: 帝為黜嘉訓，奪居相俸，允一貫歸，鯉亦同時罷。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Jiaxun, stripped Juxiang of salary, permitted Yiguan to return home; Li was dismissed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cashiered Jiaxun, fined Juxiang a year's salary, let Yiguan go home, and dismissed Li at the same time.

sentences.zh: 而一貫獨得溫旨，雖賡右之，論者益訾其有內援焉。

translations.literal: Yet Yiguan alone received warm edicts; although Geng backed him, critics increasingly reviled him as having inside backing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yiguan alone received gracious parting words; though Geng stood by him, critics increasingly said he enjoyed secret patronage at court.

sentences.zh: 一貫之入閣也，為錫爵、誌臯所薦。

translations.literal: Yiguan's entry into the Grand Secretariat had been through recommendation by Xijue and Zhigao.
translations.idiomatic: Yiguan had entered the Grand Secretariat on the recommendation of Xijue and Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 輔政十有三年，當國者四年。

translations.literal: He assisted in government for thirteen years and was in charge of state affairs for four.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Secretariat for thirteen years and actually directed policy for four.

sentences.zh: 枝拄清議，好同惡異，與前後諸臣同。

translations.literal: He propped up against pure criticism, favored agreement and hated difference, the same as ministers before and after.
translations.idiomatic: He braced himself against moral criticism, loved allies and hated dissent, no different from the ministers before and after him.

sentences.zh: 至楚宗、妖書、京察三事，獨犯不韙，論者醜之，雖其黨不能解免也。

translations.literal: But in the three affairs of the Chu princely house, the demon book, and the capital evaluation, he alone committed notorious wrongs; critics reviled him, and even his faction could not clear him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Chu princely dispute, the Demon Book case, and the capital evaluation he alone crossed lines no one could defend; even his own faction could not excuse him.

sentences.zh: 一貫歸，言者追劾之不已，其鄉人亦多受世詆諆雲。

translations.literal: After Yiguan returned home, remonstrance officials pursued impeachment without cease, and many of his fellow-townsmen too suffered worldly slander.
translations.idiomatic: After he went home, censors kept impeaching him, and many of his countrymen bore the world's scorn as well.

sentences.zh: 一貫在位，累加少傅兼太子太傅、吏部尚書、建極殿大學士。

translations.literal: While in office he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Tutor concurrent with Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Academician of the Jianji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In office he rose through Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent to Minister of Personnel and Grand Academician of the Jianji Hall.

sentences.zh: 家居十年卒。

translations.literal: After ten years at home he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died ten years after retiring.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and given the temple name Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the temple name Wengong.

sentences.zh: 方從哲

translations.literal: Fang Congzhe
translations.idiomatic: Fang Congzhe

sentences.zh: 方從哲，字中涵，其先德清人。

translations.literal: Fang Congzhe, style Zhonghan, his ancestors were men of Deqing.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Congzhe, courtesy name Zhonghan, came originally from Deqing.

sentences.zh: 隸籍錦衣衛，家京師。

translations.literal: Registered in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, the family dwelt in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The family was registered with the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and lived in the capital.

sentences.zh: 從哲登萬歷十一年進士，授庶吉士，屢遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Congzhe passed the civil examination in the eleventh year of Wanli, was appointed Hanlin bachelor, and was repeatedly promoted to Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 11, entered the Hanlin Academy, and rose step by step to Chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 請告家居，久不出，時頗稱其恬雅。

translations.literal: He requested leave to live at home, long did not emerge, and at the time was somewhat praised for quiet elegance.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire home, stayed away for years, and was praised at the time for his quiet, refined manner.

sentences.zh: 大學士葉向高請用為禮部右侍郎，不報。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao requested appointing him Vice Minister of Rites; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao asked to appoint him Vice Minister of Rites, but the throne did not answer.

sentences.zh: 中旨起吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: An imperial command summoned him as Vice Minister of Personnel on the left.
translations.idiomatic: An edict from the palace summoned him as Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 為給事中李成名所劾，求罷，不允。

translations.literal: He was impeached by supervising secretary Li Chengming, sought dismissal, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Li Chengming impeached him; he asked to resign and was refused.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，拜禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，與吳道南並命。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was appointed Minister of Rites concurrent with Grand Academician of the Eastern Hall, appointed together with Wu Daonan.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he was made Minister of Rites and Grand Academician of the Eastern Hall, appointed on the same day as Wu Daonan.

sentences.zh: 時道南在籍，向高為首輔，政事多決於向高。

translations.literal: At the time Daonan was on leave in his native place; Xianggao was chief minister and most government affairs were decided by Xianggao.
translations.idiomatic: Daonan was then at home on leave; Xianggao was chief minister and most affairs still rested with him.

sentences.zh: 向高去國，從哲遂獨相。

translations.literal: When Xianggao left office, Congzhe then became sole prime minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianggao left office, Congzhe became the sole Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 請召還舊輔沈鯉，不允。

translations.literal: He requested recalling the former assistant minister Shen Li; not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to recall the former Grand Secretary Shen Li; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 御史錢春劾其容悅，從哲乞罷。

translations.literal: Censor Qian Chun impeached his ingratiating manner; Congzhe begged dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Qian Chun impeached him for fawning; Congzhe asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝優旨慰留。

translations.literal: The emperor issued kind words of consolation and kept him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent warm words of comfort and kept him in post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，道南至。

translations.literal: Before long Daonan arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Daonan took up his post.

sentences.zh: 會張差梃擊事起，刑部以瘋癲蔽獄。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cha's club assault affair arose, the Ministry of Punishments covered the case with plea of madness.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cha's stick attack on the heir apparent occurred, the Ministry of Punishments buried the case under a verdict of insanity.

sentences.zh: 王之寀鉤得其情，龐保、劉成等跡始露。

translations.literal: Wang Zhicai traced out the facts, and the tracks of Pang Bao, Liu Cheng, and others began to show.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhicai dug out the truth, and the trail led toward Pang Bao, Liu Cheng, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 從哲偕道南斥之寀言謬妄，帝納之。

translations.literal: Congzhe together with Daonan dismissed Zhicai's words as wild and absurd; the emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe and Daonan called Zhicai's account absurd; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 道南為言路所詆，求去者經歲，以母憂歸。

translations.literal: Daonan was reviled by the remonstrance corps, sought departure for a full year, and returned home on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Daonan was torn apart by the censorate, begged to leave for a year, and went home when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 從哲復獨相，即疏請推補閣臣。

translations.literal: Congzhe again became sole prime minister and at once memorialized requesting supplementary appointment of Grand Secretariat members.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe was alone at the helm again and at once memorialized to fill the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自後每月必請。

translations.literal: From then on he requested every month without fail.
translations.idiomatic: After that he asked every month without fail.

sentences.zh: 帝以一人足辦，迄不增置。

translations.literal: The emperor thought one man was enough to manage affairs and to the end did not add more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decided one man was enough and never added another.

sentences.zh: 從哲性柔懦，不能任大事。

translations.literal: Congzhe was by nature soft and timid and could not undertake great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe was gentle and timid by nature and could not bear heavy burdens.

sentences.zh: 時東宮久輟講，瑞王婚禮逾期，惠王、桂王未擇配，福府莊田遣中使督賦，又議令鬻鹽，中旨命呂貴督織造，駙馬王昺以救劉光復褫冠帶，山東盜起，災異數見，言官翟鳳翀、郭尚賓以直言貶，帝遣中使令工部侍郎林如楚繕修咸安營，宣府缺餉數月，從哲皆上疏力言，帝多不聽。

translations.literal: At the time lectures for the Eastern Palace had long been suspended; the Rui Prince's wedding was overdue; the Hui and Gui princes had not yet been matched in marriage; for the Fu princely establishment's estate lands eunuchs were dispatched to supervise collection; sale of salt was also debated; an imperial command appointed Lü Gui to supervise weaving manufacture; royal son-in-law Wang Bing was stripped of cap and belt for rescuing Liu Guangfu; bandits rose in Shandong; strange portents appeared repeatedly; remonstrance officials Zhai Fengchong and Guo Shangbin were demoted for straight speaking; the emperor sent eunuchs ordering Vice Minister of Works Lin Ruchu to repair the Xian'an camp; Xuanfu lacked pay for several months—Congzhe memorialized forcefully on all these, and the emperor mostly would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Lectures for the crown prince had long ceased; the Rui Prince's wedding dragged past its date; the Hui and Gui princes still had no consorts; eunuchs were sent to squeeze the Fu princely estates; the court debated selling salt by decree; Lü Gui was ordered to run the imperial workshops; the consort's son-in-law Wang Bing lost his rank for saving Liu Guangfu; bandits rose in Shandong; omens multiplied; censors Zhai Fengchong and Guo Shangbin were banished for blunt speech; eunuchs ordered Lin Ruchu to rebuild the Xian'an barracks; Xuanfu went months without pay—on every one of these Congzhe memorialized in protest, and the emperor usually ignored him.

sentences.zh: 而從哲有內援，以名爭而已，實將順帝意，無所匡正。

translations.literal: Yet Congzhe had inside backing and contested in name only; in fact he followed the emperor's will and corrected nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Congzhe had patrons behind the screen: he argued in public but in truth followed the emperor's mood and corrected nothing.

sentences.zh: 向高秉政時，黨論鼎沸。

translations.literal: When Xianggao held power, faction rhetoric boiled over.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianggao, factional warfare boiled over.

sentences.zh: 言路交通銓部，指清流為東林，逐之殆盡。

translations.literal: The remonstrance corps colluded with the appointment ministries, labeled the pure current as Donglin, and nearly drove them all out.
translations.idiomatic: Censors colluded with the appointment offices, tagged the moralists as Donglin, and nearly drove them from court.

sentences.zh: 及從哲秉政，言路已無正人，黨論漸息。

translations.literal: When Congzhe held power, the remonstrance corps already had no upright men; faction rhetoric gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Under Congzhe the censorate already held no honest men, and partisan shouting slowly died down.

sentences.zh: 丁巳京察，盡斥東林，且及林居者。

translations.literal: In the dingsi capital evaluation, Donglin men were entirely expelled, including those living in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingsi evaluation of capital officials, Donglin men were cleared out entirely, even those living in retirement.

sentences.zh: 齊、楚、浙三黨鼎立，務搏擊清流。

translations.literal: The Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions stood as three pillars, bent on attacking the pure current.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions formed a tripod of power and set themselves to crush the moralists.

sentences.zh: 齊人亓詩教，從哲門生，勢尤張。

translations.literal: Qi man Qi Shijiao, Congzhe's student, held power especially broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shijiao of the Qi faction, Congzhe's own student, wielded power above all.

sentences.zh: 從哲昵群小，而帝怠荒亦益甚。

translations.literal: Congzhe was intimate with petty men, and the emperor's neglect grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe clung to small men, and the emperor's indifference deepened.

sentences.zh: 畿輔、山東、山西、河南、江西及大江南北相繼告災，疏皆不發。

translations.literal: Capital region, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, and north and south of the Yangtze reported disasters in succession; memorials were all not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The capital districts, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, and lands north and south of the Yangtze sent disaster reports one after another, and none of the memorials were released.

sentences.zh: 舊制，給事中五十余員，御史百余員。

translations.literal: Under the old system there were more than fifty supervising secretaries and more than a hundred censors.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom there had been more than fifty supervising secretaries and more than a hundred censors.

sentences.zh: 至是六科止四人，而五科印無所屬；

translations.literal: By now only four of the Six Offices remained, and the seals of the five offices had no holder;
translations.idiomatic: Now only four of the Six Offices still had officers, and five offices had no one to hold their seals;

sentences.zh: 十三道止五人，一人領數職。

translations.literal: only five of the thirteen circuits remained, one man holding several posts.
translations.idiomatic: only five of the thirteen surveillance circuits were staffed, with one man covering several posts.

sentences.zh: 在外巡按率不得代。

translations.literal: Outside the capital, touring censors generally could not be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial touring censors could seldom be replaced when their terms ended.

sentences.zh: 六部堂上官僅四五人，都御史數年空署，督撫監司亦屢缺不補。

translations.literal: Only four or five department heads in the Six Ministries; for several years the post of Censor-in-Chief stood empty; governors-general, governors, and surveillance commissioners were also often unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Ministries had only four or five department heads; the Censor-in-Chief's post stood empty for years; governors, grand coordinators, and surveillance commissioners went long unfilled.

sentences.zh: 文武大選、急選官及四方教職，積數千人，以吏、兵二科缺掌印不畫憑，久滯都下，時攀執政輿哀訴。

translations.literal: Civil and military great selections, urgent selections, and local education officials—several thousand persons—because the Personnel and War sections lacked seal-holders and would not sign credentials, long lingered in the capital, at times clinging to the prime minister's carriage wailing their grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of candidates for civil and military posts, urgent appointments, and local teaching posts, because the Personnel and War supervising offices had no seal-holder and would not sign commissions, rotted in the capital and sometimes threw themselves before the Grand Secretary's carriage, wailing.

sentences.zh: 詔獄囚以理刑無人不決遣，家屬聚號長安門。

translations.literal: Prisoners in the imperial prison, for want of staff in the Ministry of Justice, went undecided and undispatched; families gathered crying at Chang'an Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners in the imperial prison, with no one in the Ministry of Justice to judge them, went un-sentenced; their families crowded Chang'an Gate, weeping.

sentences.zh: 職業盡弛，上下解體。

translations.literal: Duties were wholly neglected; court and countryside fell apart.
translations.idiomatic: Every office slackened; above and below the realm came undone.

sentences.zh: 四十六年四月，大清兵克撫順，朝野震驚。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, fourth month, Qing forces captured Fushun; court and countryside were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the forty-sixth year Qing troops took Fushun, and the whole court trembled.

sentences.zh: 帝初頗憂懼，章奏時下，不數月泄泄如故。

translations.literal: At first the emperor was somewhat worried and fearful; memorials were sometimes issued; within a few months he was slack as before.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor seemed uneasy and memorials actually moved; within a few months he was as indifferent as ever.

sentences.zh: 從哲子世鴻殺人，巡城御史劾之。

translations.literal: Congzhe's son Shihong killed a man; the city-patrol censor impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe's son Shihong killed a man, and the city-patrol censor impeached him.

sentences.zh: 從哲乞罷，不允。

translations.literal: Congzhe begged dismissal; not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe asked to resign; the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 長星見東南，長二丈，廣尺余，十有九日而滅。

translations.literal: A long comet appeared in the southeast, two zhang in length and more than a foot wide, and vanished after nineteen days.
translations.idiomatic: A long-tailed comet showed in the southeast, two zhang long and more than a foot across, and faded after nineteen days.

sentences.zh: 是日京師地震。

translations.literal: That day the capital region shook in an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the capital was shaken by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 從哲言：「妖象怪徵，層見疊出，除臣奉職無狀痛自修省外，望陛下大奮乾綱，與天下更始。

translations.literal: Congzhe said: "Omens and strange signs appear layer upon layer; apart from my own incompetence in office, for which I bitterly reproach myself, I hope Your Majesty will greatly rouse imperial authority and begin anew with the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe wrote: "Strange omens pile one on another. Leaving aside my own failure in office, which I reproach bitterly, I beg Your Majesty to rouse the imperial will and make a fresh start with the empire.

sentences.zh: 」朝士雜然笑之。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen laughed in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Men at court laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 帝亦不省。

translations.literal: The emperor too took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, too, paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 御史熊化以時事多艱、佐理無效劾從哲，乞用災異策免。

translations.literal: Censor Xiong Hua impeached Congzhe because the times were hard and his assistance ineffective, asking that he be removed by the policy of responding to calamities and omens.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xiong Hua impeached Congzhe, saying the times were dire and his aid useless, and begged the throne to dismiss him under the ancient rule of answering omens with policy change.

sentences.zh: 從哲懇求罷，堅臥四十余日，閣中虛無人。

translations.literal: Congzhe earnestly begged to resign and lay abed more than forty days; the Grand Secretariat stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe pleaded to resign and stayed in bed more than forty days, leaving the Grand Secretariat empty.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留再三，乃起視事。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly comforted and retained him; only then did he rise to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him again and again until he rose and returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，楊鎬四路出師，兵科給事中趙興邦用紅旗督戰，師大敗。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year Yang Hao sent armies out by four routes; supervising secretary Zhao Xingbang of the War Section used a red flag to supervise battle; the army suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, Yang Hao marched four armies; War Section secretary Zhao Xingbang waved a red flag to hurry them into battle, and the forces were shattered.

sentences.zh: 禮部主事夏嘉遇謂遼事之壞，由興邦及從哲庇李維翰所致，兩疏劾之。

translations.literal: Section chief Xia Jiayu of the Ministry of Rites said the ruin of Liaodong affairs was caused by Xingbang and Congzhe's shielding of Li Weihan, and submitted two memorials impeaching them.
translations.idiomatic: Rites section chief Xia Jiayu blamed the Liaodong disaster on Xingbang and on Congzhe for protecting Li Weihan, and impeached both in two memorials.

sentences.zh: 眾哲求罷，不敢入閣，視事於朝房。

translations.literal: Congzhe begged to resign, dared not enter the Grand Secretariat, and conducted business in the morning session room.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe asked to quit, refused to enter the Secretariat, and held court from the morning session room instead.

sentences.zh: 帝優旨懇留，乃復故，而反擢興邦為太常少卿。

translations.literal: The emperor issued kind words earnestly retaining him; he then returned to his former post, yet in turn promoted Xingbang to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent gracious words urging him to stay; he returned to office, while Xingbang was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大清兵連克開原、鐵嶺。

translations.literal: Before long Qing forces in succession captured Kaiyuan and Tieling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qing troops took Kaiyuan and Tieling in succession.

sentences.zh: 廷臣於文華門拜疏，立請批發，又候旨思善門，皆不報。

translations.literal: Court ministers presented memorials at the Wenhua Gate, immediately requesting promulgation, and again waited for edicts at the Sishan Gate—all without response.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers offered memorials at the Wenhua Gate and pressed for immediate reply; they waited at the Sishan Gate for imperial word—and heard nothing.

sentences.zh: 從哲乃叩首仁德門跪俟俞旨，帝終不報。

translations.literal: Congzhe thereupon kowtowed at the Rende Gate and knelt awaiting approval; the emperor to the end gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe kowtowed at the Rende Gate and knelt for an answer; the emperor never replied.

sentences.zh: 俄請帝出御文華殿，召見群臣，面商戰守方略。

translations.literal: Shortly he asked the emperor to come out and preside at the Wenhua Hall, summon the ministers, and discuss strategy of war and defense face to face.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked the emperor to appear at the Wenhua Hall, summon the ministers, and debate war and defense in person.

sentences.zh: 亦不報。

translations.literal: Again no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Again there was no answer.

sentences.zh: 請補閣臣疏十上，情極哀，始命廷推。

translations.literal: Memorials requesting supplementary appointment of Grand Secretariat members were submitted ten times in extreme grief; only then was court recommendation ordered.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized ten times in desperate tones to fill the Grand Secretariat before the throne ordered a court recommendation.

sentences.zh: 及推上，又不用。

translations.literal: When the recommendations were submitted, again they were not used.
translations.idiomatic: When the names came up, the emperor still would not appoint them.

sentences.zh: 從哲復連請，乃簡用史繼偕、沈纮，疏仍留中，終帝世寢不下。

translations.literal: Congzhe again petitioned in succession; only then were Shi Jixie and Shen Hong selected, yet the memorial was still held in the palace and to the end of the emperor's reign was shelved and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe pressed again and again until Shi Jixie and Shen Hong were chosen, but the appointment memorial stayed in the palace and was never issued before Shenzong died.

sentences.zh: 御史張新詔劾從哲諸所疏揭，委罪君父，誑言欺人，祖宗二百年金甌壞從哲手。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Xin'ao impeached all Congzhe's open memorials, saying he shifted blame onto ruler and father, deceived with false words, and that the two-hundred-year golden vessel of the ancestors was broken in Congzhe's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Xin'ao attacked Congzhe's public memorials as shifting blame onto the throne, lying to the court, and shattering the two-hundred-year vessel of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 御史蕭毅中、劉蔚、周方鑒、楊春茂、王尊德、左光鬥，山西參政徐如翰亦交章擊之。

translations.literal: Censors Xiao Yizhong, Liu Wei, Zhou Fangjian, Yang Chunmao, Wang Zunde, and Zuo Guangdou, and Shanxi Administration Commissioner Xu Ruhang, also submitted linked memorials attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Xiao Yizhong, Liu Wei, Zhou Fangjian, Yang Chunmao, Wang Zunde, and Zuo Guangdou, with Shanxi commissioner Xu Ruhang, piled on with joint attacks.

sentences.zh: 從哲連疏自明，且乞罷。

translations.literal: Congzhe submitted linked memorials clarifying himself and also begged to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe answered in a stream of memorials and again asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不問。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored it all.

sentences.zh: 自劉光復系獄，從哲論救數十疏。

translations.literal: From the time Liu Guangfu was imprisoned, Congzhe memorialized dozens of times to save him.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Guangfu was jailed, Congzhe wrote dozens of memorials pleading for him.

sentences.zh: 帝特釋為民，而用人行政諸章奏終不發。

translations.literal: The emperor specially released him to commoner status, yet memorials on personnel and administration to the end were not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally freed Liu Guangfu to civilian life, but memorials on appointments and policy were never released.

sentences.zh: 帝有疾數月。

translations.literal: The emperor had been ill for several months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been ill for months.

sentences.zh: 會皇后崩，從哲哭臨畢，請至榻前起居。

translations.literal: When the empress died, after Congzhe finished mourning attendance he asked to come before the couch to inquire after the emperor's health.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress died, Congzhe finished the mourning rites and asked to attend the emperor at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 召見弘德殿，跪語良久，因請補閣臣，用大僚，下臺諫命。

translations.literal: Summoned to the Hongde Hall, he knelt and spoke at length, then asked to supplement Grand Secretariat members, employ great ministers, and issue orders for censors and remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the Hongde Hall, he knelt and talked at length, then asked to fill the Secretariat, appoint senior ministers, and release the censors waiting for orders.

sentences.zh: 帝許之，乃叩頭出。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed; he then kowtowed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; Congzhe kowtowed and left.

sentences.zh: 帝素惡言官，前此考選除授者，率候命二三年，及是候八年。

translations.literal: The emperor had always hated remonstrance officials; those selected and appointed before this generally waited for orders two or three years, and by now waited eight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always hated censors; newly chosen men used to wait two or three years for appointment, but now they waited eight.

sentences.zh: 從哲請至數十疏，竟不下。

translations.literal: Congzhe requested to the point of dozens of memorials; in the end they were not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe memorialized dozens of times on their behalf; none of the orders were ever issued.

sentences.zh: 帝自以海宇承平，官不必備，有意損之。

translations.literal: The emperor himself thought the realm was at peace and offices need not be fully staffed, and intended to reduce them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed the realm was at peace and posts need not be filled, and meant to cut them.

sentences.zh: 及遼左軍興，又不欲矯前失，行之如舊。

translations.literal: When war arose on the eastern frontier he again did not wish to correct his earlier mistake and carried on as before.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Liaodong he would not undo his earlier mistake and kept the old ways.

sentences.zh: 從哲獨秉國成，卒無所匡救。

translations.literal: Congzhe alone held the nation's helm and in the end corrected nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe held the helm alone and in the end saved nothing.

sentences.zh: 又用姚宗文閱遼東，齮經略熊廷弼去，遼陽遂失。

translations.literal: He again used Yao Zongwen to inspect Liaodong, drove off frontier commissioner Xiong Tingbi, and Liaoyang was then lost.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yao Zongwen to inspect Liaodong, forced out frontier commissioner Xiong Tingbi, and Liaoyang fell.

sentences.zh: 論者謂明之亡，神宗實基之，而從哲其罪首也。

translations.literal: Critics said the fall of Ming was in fact founded by Shenzong, and Congzhe was the chief culprit.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Ming's fall was laid by Shenzong, with Congzhe as its chief author.

sentences.zh: 四十八年七月丙子朔，帝不豫，十有七日大漸。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, seventh month, first day of the sexagenary cycle bingzi, the emperor fell ill; after seventeen days he was critically ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the forty-eighth year, on the first day bingzi, the emperor fell ill; seventeen days later he was dying.

sentences.zh: 外廷憂危，從哲偕九卿臺諫詣思善門問安。

translations.literal: The outer court was anxious; Congzhe together with the Nine Ministers and censorate and remonstrance corps went to the Sishan Gate to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: The outer court was in dread; Congzhe went with the Nine Ministers and censors to the Sishan Gate to ask after the emperor.

sentences.zh: 越二日，召從哲及尚書周嘉謨、李汝華、黃嘉善、黃克纘等受顧命。

translations.literal: Two days later he summoned Congzhe and Ministers Zhou Jiamo, Li Ruhua, Huang Jiashan, Huang Kezuan, and others to receive the dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he summoned Congzhe and the ministers Zhou Jiamo, Li Ruhua, Huang Jiashan, Huang Kezuan, and others to receive his final charge.

sentences.zh: 又二日，乃崩。

translations.literal: Two days more, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two days after that he died.

sentences.zh: 八月丙午朔，光宗嗣位。

translations.literal: On the first day bingwu of the eighth month Guangzong succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day bingwu of the eighth month, Guangzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 鄭貴妃以前福王故，懼帝銜之，進珠玉及侍姬八人啖帝。

translations.literal: Honored Consort Zheng, because of the earlier Fu Prince, feared the emperor bore a grudge and presented pearls and jade and eight attendant maidens to please the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Zheng, mindful of the old Fu Prince affair, feared the new emperor's resentment and sent pearls, jade, and eight palace women to win him over.

sentences.zh: 選侍李氏最得帝寵，貴妃因請立選侍為皇后，選侍亦為貴妃求封太后。

translations.literal: Palace Lady Li of the Selection Quarters won the emperor's favor most; the honored consort therefore asked to make the selection lady empress, and the selection lady also asked empress dowager rank for the honored consort.
translations.idiomatic: Selection Lady Li was the emperor's favorite; Zheng asked that Li be made empress, and Li in turn asked that Zheng be made empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 帝已於乙卯得疾，丁巳力疾御門，命從哲封貴妃為皇太后，從哲遽以命禮部。

translations.literal: The emperor had already fallen ill on yimao; on dingsi he forced himself to hold court at the gate, ordered Congzhe to ennoble the honored consort as empress dowager, and Congzhe hastily passed the order to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He had fallen ill on yimao; on dingsi he dragged himself to court and told Congzhe to make Zheng empress dowager, and Congzhe at once relayed the order to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 侍郎孫如遊力爭，事乃止。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Sun Ruyou argued forcefully, and the matter then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Sun Ruyou protested fiercely, and the matter died.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，帝不視朝，從哲偕廷臣詣宮門問安。

translations.literal: On xinyou the emperor did not hold court; Congzhe together with court ministers went to the palace gate to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the emperor skipped court; Congzhe and the ministers went to the palace gate to ask after him.

sentences.zh: 時都下紛言中官崔文升進泄藥，帝由此委頓，而帝傳諭有「頭目眩暈，身體軟弱，不能動履」語，群情益疑駭。

translations.literal: At the time the capital buzzed that eunuch Cui Wensheng had administered a purgative, and the emperor was weakened thereby; yet the emperor's transmitted message had the words "head dizzy and eyes dim, body weak, unable to walk," and public feeling grew ever more suspicious and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor said eunuch Cui Wensheng had given the emperor a purgative and left him prostrate; the palace message spoke of dizziness, weakness, and inability to walk, and fear spread through the capital.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊漣劾文升，並及從哲。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Yang Lian impeached Wensheng and also touched Congzhe.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Yang Lian impeached Wensheng and implicated Congzhe as well.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事孫朝肅、徐儀世、御史鄭宗周並上書從哲，請保護聖體，速建儲貳。

translations.literal: Punishments section chief Sun Chaosu and Xu Yishi and censor Zheng Zongzhou together wrote Congzhe, asking him to protect the sacred person and quickly establish the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments chiefs Sun Chaosu and Xu Yishi and censor Zheng Zongzhou wrote Congzhe urging him to guard the emperor's health and establish the heir at once.

sentences.zh: 從哲候安，因言進藥宜慎。

translations.literal: Congzhe while waiting to inquire after health spoke of the need for caution in administering medicine.
translations.idiomatic: While waiting to inquire after the emperor, Congzhe said medicine must be chosen with care.

sentences.zh: 帝褒答之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and answered him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered him with praise.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，新閣臣劉一燝、韓爌入直，帝疾已殆。

translations.literal: On wuchen the new Grand Secretaries Liu Yijing and Han Kuang entered duty; the emperor's illness was already desperate.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the new Grand Secretaries Liu Yijing and Han Kuang took up duty; the emperor was already near death.

sentences.zh: 辛未，召從哲、一燝、爌，英國公張惟賢，吏部尚書周嘉謨，戶部尚書李汝華，禮部侍郎署部事孫如遊，刑部尚書黃克纘，左都御史張問達，給事中範濟世、楊漣，御史顧慥等至乾清宮。

translations.literal: On xinwei he summoned Congzhe, Yijing, Kuang, Duke of England Zhang Weixian, Minister of Personnel Zhou Jiamo, Minister of Revenue Li Ruhua, Vice Minister of Rites Sun Ruyou acting as head of the ministry, Minister of Punishments Huang Kezuan, Left Censor-in-Chief Zhang Wenda, supervising secretaries Fan Jishi and Yang Lian, censor Gu Zao, and others to the Qianqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he summoned Congzhe, Yijing, Kuang, the Duke of England Zhang Weixian, Zhou Jiamo, Li Ruhua, acting Minister of Rites Sun Ruyou, Huang Kezuan, Zhang Wenda, Fan Jishi, Yang Lian, Gu Zao, and the rest to the Qianqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝御東暖閣憑幾，皇長子、皇五子等皆侍。

translations.literal: The emperor sat leaning on a desk in the east warm chamber; the eldest imperial son, the fifth imperial son, and others all attended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaned on a desk in the east warm chamber while the eldest prince, the fifth prince, and others stood by.

sentences.zh: 帝命諸臣前，從哲等因請慎醫藥。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ministers forward; Congzhe and the others thereupon asked that medicine be chosen with care.
translations.idiomatic: He called the ministers forward; Congzhe and the others again urged caution with medicine.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「十余日不進矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For more than ten days I have taken nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have eaten nothing for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 」遂諭冊封選侍為皇貴妃。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered enfeoffment of the selection lady as honored consort.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he ordered the selection lady enfeoffed as honored consort.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，復召諸臣，諭冊封事。

translations.literal: On jiaxu he again summoned the ministers and spoke of the enfeoffment affair.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he summoned them again to discuss the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 從哲等請速建儲貳。

translations.literal: Congzhe and the others asked to quickly establish the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe and the others begged him to establish the heir at once.

sentences.zh: 帝顧皇長子曰：「卿等其輔為堯、舜。

translations.literal: The emperor turned to the eldest imperial son and said: "You must assist him to become Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked at the eldest prince and said, "You must help him become a Yao or a Shun.

sentences.zh: 」又語及壽宮，從哲等以先帝山陵對。

translations.literal: " He also spoke of the longevity palace; Congzhe and the others answered with the late emperor's mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: " He spoke of his tomb; Congzhe and the others answered with the late emperor's mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝自指曰：「朕壽宮也。

translations.literal: The emperor pointed to himself and said: "My longevity palace is here.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pointed at himself and said, "My tomb is here.

sentences.zh: 」諸臣皆泣。

translations.literal: " All the ministers wept.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministers wept.

sentences.zh: 帝復問：「有鴻臚官進藥者安在？

translations.literal: The emperor again asked: "Where is the Court of Imperial Entertainments official who presented medicine?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "Where is the Court of Imperial Entertainments man who offered medicine?

sentences.zh: 」從哲曰：「鴻臚寺丞李可灼自雲仙方，臣等未敢信。

translations.literal: " Congzhe said: "Court of Imperial Entertainments Assistant Director Li Kezhuo claims an immortal formula of his own; we ministers have not dared believe it.
translations.idiomatic: " Congzhe said, "Assistant Director Li Kezhuo claims an immortal formula; we have not dared trust it.

sentences.zh: 」帝命宣可灼至，趣和藥進，所謂紅丸者也。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered Kezhuo summoned, urged him to mix the medicine and present it—the so-called red pills.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered Kezhuo brought in, told him to mix the dose and present it—the so-called red pills.

sentences.zh: 帝服訖，稱「忠臣」者再。

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished taking it, he twice called him "loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor swallowed it, he twice called Kezhuo a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 諸臣出俟宮門外。

translations.literal: The ministers went out and waited outside the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers withdrew and waited outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 頃之，中使傳上體平善。

translations.literal: Shortly a messenger reported the emperor's condition peaceful and good.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a messenger said the emperor felt better.

sentences.zh: 日晡，可灼出，言復進一丸。

translations.literal: At sunset Kezhuo came out and said he would present another pill.
translations.idiomatic: At sunset Kezhuo came out and said he would give another pill.

sentences.zh: 從哲等問狀，曰：「平善如前。

translations.literal: Congzhe and the others asked the condition; he said: "Peaceful and good as before.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe and the others asked how the emperor was; Kezhuo said, "Well, as before.

sentences.zh: 」明日九月乙亥朔卯刻，帝崩。

translations.literal: " The next day, first day of the ninth month yihai at the mao hour, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day, at dawn on the first day of the ninth month, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 中外皆恨可灼甚，而從哲擬遺旨賚可灼銀幣。

translations.literal: Inside and outside all hated Kezhuo bitterly, yet Congzhe drafted the dying charge to reward Kezhuo with silver and coins.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country loathed Kezhuo, yet Congzhe drafted a posthumous order to reward him with silver.

sentences.zh: 時李選侍居乾清宮，群臣入臨，諸閹閉宮門不許入。

translations.literal: At the time Selection Lady Li dwelt in the Qianqing Palace; when the ministers entered to mourn, the eunuchs closed the palace gate and would not let them in.
translations.idiomatic: Selection Lady Li still occupied the Qianqing Palace; when ministers came to mourn, eunuchs shut the gate and kept them out.

sentences.zh: 劉一燝、楊漣力拄之，得哭臨如禮，擁皇長子出居慈慶宮。

translations.literal: Liu Yijing and Yang Lian forcefully resisted them, obtained mourning according to ritual, and escorted the eldest imperial son out to dwell in the Ciqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yijing and Yang Lian forced the issue, secured a proper mourning, and escorted the eldest prince to the Ciqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 從哲委蛇而已。

translations.literal: Congzhe only equivocated.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe only wavered.

sentences.zh: 初，鄭貴妃居乾清宮侍神宗疾，光宗即位猶未遷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Honored Consort Zheng had dwelt in the Qianqing Palace attending Shenzong's illness; when Guangzong took the throne she had still not moved.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zheng had stayed in the Qianqing Palace nursing Shenzong; even after Guangzong's accession she had not moved out.

sentences.zh: 尚書嘉謨責貴妃從子養性，乃遷慈寧宮。

translations.literal: Minister Jiamo reproved the honored consort's nephew Yang Xing, and only then did she move to the Cining Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Jiamo rebuked Zheng's nephew Yang Xing, and only then did she move to the Cining Palace.

sentences.zh: 及光宗崩，而李選侍居乾清宮。

translations.literal: When Guangzong died, Selection Lady Li dwelt in the Qianqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong died, Selection Lady Li held the Qianqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 給事中漣及御史左光鬥念選侍嘗邀封後，非可令居乾清，以沖主付托也。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Lian and censor Zuo Guangdou reflected that the selection lady had once sought the title of empress and could not be allowed to dwell in the Qianqing Palace, where the young sovereign would be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou recalled that Li had once sought to be empress and should not hold the Qianqing Palace where the young emperor would live.

sentences.zh: 於是議移宮，爭數日不決。

translations.literal: Thereupon they debated moving the palace; the dispute went on several days without decision.
translations.idiomatic: They debated moving her out, and the quarrel dragged on for days.

sentences.zh: 從哲欲徐之。

translations.literal: Congzhe wished to proceed slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe wanted to go slowly.

sentences.zh: 至登極前一日，一燝、爌邀從哲立宮門請，選侍乃移噦鸞宮。

translations.literal: Down to the day before the enthronement, Yijing and Kuang invited Congzhe to stand at the palace gate and request it; only then did the selection lady move to the Huanyuan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the eve of enthronement did Yijing and Kuang get Congzhe to stand at the gate and demand it; then Li moved to the Huanyuan Palace.

sentences.zh: 明日庚辰，熹宗即位。

translations.literal: The next day gengchen, Xizong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, gengchen, Xizong was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 先是，御史王安舜劾從哲輕薦狂醫，又賞之以自掩。

translations.literal: Earlier, censor Wang Anshun impeached Congzhe for lightly recommending a mad physician and again rewarding him to cover himself.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier censor Wang Anshun had impeached Congzhe for trusting a quack doctor and rewarding him to cover his tracks.

sentences.zh: 從哲擬太子令旨，罰可灼俸一年。

translations.literal: Congzhe drafted the heir apparent's order and fined Kezhuo one year's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe drafted an order in the heir's name fining Kezhuo one year's salary.

sentences.zh: 御史鄭宗周劾文升罪，請下法司，從哲擬令旨司禮察處。

translations.literal: Censor Zheng Zongzhou impeached Wensheng's crime and asked to send him to the judicial offices; Congzhe drafted an order for the Directorate of Ceremonies to investigate and dispose.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zheng Zongzhou demanded Wensheng be sent to the courts; Congzhe drafted an order for the eunuch directorate to investigate.

sentences.zh: 及御史郭如楚、馮三元、焦源溥，給事中魏應嘉，太常卿曹光，光祿少卿高攀龍，主事呂維祺，先後上疏言：「可灼罪不容誅，從哲庇之，國法安在！

translations.literal: When censors Guo Ruchu, Feng Sanyuan, and Jiao Yuanpu, supervising secretary Wei Yingjia, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Cao Guang, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Gao Panlong, and section chief Lü Weiqi successively submitted memorials saying: "Kezhuo's crime brooks no execution, yet Congzhe shields him—where is the law of the state!
translations.idiomatic: Censors Guo Ruchu, Feng Sanyuan, and Jiao Yuanpu, secretary Wei Yingjia, Director Cao Guang, Vice Director Gao Panlong, and chief Lü Weiqi wrote in turn: "Kezhuo deserves death, yet Congzhe shields him—where is the law of the state!

sentences.zh: 」而給事中惠世揚直糾從哲十罪、三可殺。

translations.literal: " Supervising secretary Hui Shiyang directly impeached Congzhe with ten crimes and three grounds for execution.
translations.idiomatic: " Supervising secretary Hui Shiyang then charged Congzhe with ten crimes and three capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 言：「從哲獨相七年，妨賢病國，罪一。

translations.literal: He said: "Congzhe served as sole prime minister for seven years, obstructing the worthy and harming the state—crime one.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Congzhe ruled alone for seven years, blocking the worthy and sickening the state—first crime.

sentences.zh: 驕蹇無禮，失誤哭臨，罪二。

translations.literal: Arrogant and rude without propriety, erring in mourning attendance—crime two.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant, rude, and careless at the mourning rites—second crime.

sentences.zh: 梃擊青宮，庇護奸黨，罪三。

translations.literal: The club assault on the Eastern Palace, shielding wicked partisans—crime three.
translations.idiomatic: Shielding the culprits of the stick attack on the crown prince—third crime.

sentences.zh: 恣行胸臆，破壞絲綸，罪四。

translations.literal: Doing as he pleased, destroying imperial edicts—crime four.
translations.idiomatic: Doing as he pleased and wrecking imperial edicts—fourth crime.

sentences.zh: 縱子殺人，蔑視憲典，罪五。

translations.literal: Allowing his son to kill a man and despising the statutes—crime five.
translations.idiomatic: Letting his son kill a man and scorning the law—fifth crime.

sentences.zh: 阻抑言官，蔽壅耳目，罪六。

translations.literal: Suppressing remonstrance officials and blocking the ears and eyes—crime six.
translations.idiomatic: Suppressing censors and blocking the throne's ears—sixth crime.

sentences.zh: 陷城失律，寬議撫臣，罪七。

translations.literal: Losing cities and violating discipline, leniently treating frontier grand coordinators—crime seven.
translations.idiomatic: Losing cities yet going easy on frontier governors—seventh crime.

sentences.zh: 馬上催戰，覆沒全師，罪八。

translations.literal: Urging battle from horseback, destroying the whole army—crime eight.
translations.idiomatic: Urging rash battle and wiping out whole armies—eighth crime.

sentences.zh: 徇私罔上，鼎鉉貽羞，罪九。

translations.literal: Showing favoritism and deceiving the throne, shaming the chief ministers—crime nine.
translations.idiomatic: Favoring cronies and deceiving the throne, shaming the chief ministers—ninth crime.

sentences.zh: 代營榷稅，蠹國殃民，罪十。

translations.literal: Running monopoly taxes on the state's behalf, harming the state and ruining the people—crime ten.
translations.idiomatic: Running monopoly taxes for private gain, ruining state and people—tenth crime.

sentences.zh: 貴妃求封後，舉朝力爭，從哲依違兩可，當誅者一。

translations.literal: When the honored consort sought the title of empress the whole court argued forcefully; Congzhe wavered between yes and no—first ground for execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng sought to be empress the whole court protested, yet Congzhe wavered—first capital offense.

sentences.zh: 李選侍乃鄭氏私人，抗淩聖母，飲恨而沒。

translations.literal: Selection Lady Li was a private creature of the Zheng clan, resisted and insulted the empress mother, and died nursing hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Selection Lady Li was Zheng's creature, had defied the empress dowager, and died full of spite.

sentences.zh: 從哲受劉遜、李進忠所盜美珠，欲封選侍為貴妃，又聽其久據乾清，當誅者二。

translations.literal: Congzhe accepted the fine pearls stolen by Liu Xun and Li Jinzhong, wished to ennoble the selection lady as honored consort, and again allowed her long occupation of the Qianqing Palace—second ground for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe took stolen pearls from Liu Xun and Li Jinzhong, meant to make Li an honored consort, and let her hold the Qianqing Palace—second capital offense.

sentences.zh: 崔文升用泄藥傷損先帝，諸臣論之，從哲擬脫罪，李可灼進劫藥，從哲擬賞賚，當誅者三。

translations.literal: Cui Wensheng used a purgative and harmed the late emperor; when the ministers discussed it Congzhe drafted acquittal; Li Kezhuo presented destructive medicine and Congzhe drafted reward—third ground for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wensheng's purgative had harmed the late emperor, yet Congzhe drafted his release; Kezhuo's pills had killed the emperor, yet Congzhe drafted a reward—third capital offense.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，責世楊輕詆。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, Shiyang was rebuked for slighting and slandering.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, Hui Shiyang was rebuked for slander.

sentences.zh: 從哲累求去，皆慰留。

translations.literal: Congzhe repeatedly asked to leave and was each time urged to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe begged repeatedly to resign and was each time pressed to remain.

sentences.zh: 已而張潑、袁化中、王允成等連劾之，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Po, Yuan Huazhong, Wang Yuncheng, and others memorialized against him in succession; none was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Po, Yuan Huazhong, Wang Yuncheng, and others impeached him in turn; the throne would not listen.

sentences.zh: 其冬，給事中程註復劾之，從哲力求去，疏六上。

translations.literal: That winter Supervising Secretary Cheng Zhu impeached him again; Congzhe strove to leave and submitted six memorials.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Cheng Zhu impeached him again; Congzhe filed six resignation memorials.

sentences.zh: 命進中極殿大學士，賚銀幣、蟒衣，遣行人護歸。

translations.literal: He was ordered advanced to Grand Secretary of the Zhongji Hall, granted silver, silks, and python robes, and sent home under escort of a courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Zhongji Hall, given silver, silks, and python robes, and sent home with an imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年四月，禮部尚書孫慎行追論可灼進紅丸，斥從哲為弒逆。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Tianqi, Minister of Rites Sun Shenxing reopened the case of Kezhuo's red pill and denounced Congzhe as regicide.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2, fourth month, Sun Shenxing reopened the red-pill case and called Congzhe a regicide.

sentences.zh: 詔廷臣議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered court officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a court debate.

sentences.zh: 都御史鄒元標主慎行疏。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zou Yuanbiao upheld Shenxing's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zou Yuanbiao backed Shenxing.

sentences.zh: 從哲疏辨，自請削官階，投四裔。

translations.literal: Congzhe memorialized in defense and asked that his rank be stripped and he be banished to the four borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe defended himself and asked to be stripped of rank and exiled.

sentences.zh: 帝慰諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him with an edict.

sentences.zh: 給事中魏大中以九卿議久稽，趣之上。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wei Zhongyi, because the Nine Ministers' deliberation had long stalled, urged that it be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongyi pressed for a decision because the Nine Ministers had delayed too long.

sentences.zh: 廷臣多主慎行，罪從哲，惟刑部尚書黃克纘，御史王誌道、徐景濂，給事中汪慶百右從哲，而詹事公鼐持兩端。

translations.literal: Most court officials upheld Shenxing and condemned Congzhe; only Minister of Punishments Huang Kexuan, censors Wang Zhidao and Xu Jinglian, and supervising secretary Wang Qingbai sided with Congzhe, while Grand Mentor Gong Tai sat on the fence.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials backed Shenxing against Congzhe; only Huang Kexuan, Wang Zhidao, Xu Jinglian, and Wang Qingbai defended him, while Gong Tai wavered.

sentences.zh: 時大學士爌述進藥始末，為從哲解。

translations.literal: At this time Grand Secretary Huang Kuang described how the medicine had been administered and excused Congzhe.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Huang Kuang then explained how the medicine had been given and spoke for Congzhe.

sentences.zh: 於是吏部尚書張問達會戶部尚書汪應蛟合奏言：「進藥始末，臣等共聞見。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister of Personnel Zhang Wenda jointly memorialized with Minister of Revenue Wang Yingjiao: "We all witnessed how the medicine was given.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenda and Wang Yingjiao jointly reported: "We all saw what happened with the medicine.

sentences.zh: 輔臣視皇考疾，急迫倉皇，弒逆二字何忍言。

translations.literal: The chief minister, seeing the late emperor's illness, was urgent and flustered—how could the word regicide be borne?
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister, seeing the emperor's sudden illness, was frantic—how could we speak of regicide?

sentences.zh: 但可灼非醫官，且非知脈知醫者。

translations.literal: Yet Kezhuo was not a medical officer and knew neither pulses nor medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhuo was no physician and knew nothing of pulses or drugs.

sentences.zh: 以藥嘗試，先帝龍馭即上升。

translations.literal: He tried the medicine experimentally, and the late emperor's dragon carriage immediately ascended.
translations.idiomatic: He experimented with the drug, and the late emperor died at once.

sentences.zh: 從哲與臣等九卿未能止，均有罪，乃反賚可灼。

translations.literal: Congzhe and we Nine Ministers could not stop it—all are guilty—yet Kezhuo was rewarded instead.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe and the Nine Ministers could not stop him—we share guilt—yet Kezhuo was rewarded.

sentences.zh: 及御史安舜有言，止令養病去，罰太輕，何以慰皇考，服中外。

translations.literal: When Censor An Shun spoke, Kezhuo was only told to go home on medical leave—a penalty too light to console the late emperor or satisfy court and country.
translations.idiomatic: When An Shun spoke up, Kezhuo was merely sent home to nurse illness—too light to satisfy the court.

sentences.zh: 宜如從哲請，削其官階，為法任咎。

translations.literal: Congzhe's request should be followed: strip his rank and let him bear the legal blame.
translations.idiomatic: We should strip Congzhe's rank as he asked and let law assign blame.

sentences.zh: 至可灼罪不可勝誅，而文升當皇考哀感傷寒時，進大黃涼藥，罪又在可灼上。

translations.literal: Kezhuo's crime is beyond execution, but when Wensheng gave a heavy cooling drug while the late emperor was grieving with cold injury, his crime ranks above Kezhuo's.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhuo deserves death; Wensheng, who gave cooling drugs when the emperor had cold injury from mourning, ranks even higher.

sentences.zh: 法皆宜顯僇，以泄公憤。

translations.literal: By law both should be publicly executed to vent public rage."
translations.idiomatic: Both should be executed publicly to appease outrage."

sentences.zh: 」議上，可灼遣戍，文升放南京，而從哲不罪。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, Kezhuo was sent to the frontier and Wensheng banished to Nanjing, but Congzhe was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhuo was exiled and Wensheng sent to Nanjing; Congzhe went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 無何，慎行引疾去。

translations.literal: Before long Shenxing left office citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shenxing resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 五年，魏忠賢輯「梃擊」、「紅丸」、「移宮」三事為《三朝要典》，以傾正人，遂免可灼戍，命文升督漕運。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Wei Zhongxian compiled the Three Cases of the Club Assault, Red Pill, and Palace Move into the Record of Three Reigns Essentials to crush upright men; Kezhuo's exile was lifted and Wensheng ordered to supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 5 Wei Zhongxian compiled the Three Cases to crush upright officials; Kezhuo's exile was revoked and Wensheng put in charge of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 其黨徐大化請起從哲，從哲不出。

translations.literal: His partisan Xu Dahua asked that Congzhe be recalled; Congzhe would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Partisan Xu Dahua asked to recall Congzhe; he refused.

sentences.zh: 然一時請誅從哲者貶殺略盡矣。

translations.literal: Yet by then those who had called for Congzhe's execution had been demoted or killed almost to a man.
translations.idiomatic: By then those who had demanded Congzhe's death had been demoted or killed almost entirely.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年二月，從哲卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Chongzhen, Congzhe died.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1, second month, Congzhe died.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文端。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 三月，下文升獄，戍南京。

translations.literal: In the third month Wensheng was imprisoned and exiled to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Wensheng was jailed and exiled to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 沈㴶，字銘縝，烏程人。

translations.literal: Shen Que, styled Mingzhen, was a native of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Que, style name Mingzhen, came from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 父節甫，字以安。

translations.literal: His father Jiefu, styled Yi'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiefu, style name Yi'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Jiajing 38.

sentences.zh: 授禮部儀制主事，厲祠祭郎中。

translations.literal: Appointed Director in the Bureau of Rites of the Ministry of Rites, he served as Director in the Bureau of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director in the Ministry of Rites' bureaus of ritual and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 詔建祠禁內，令黃冠祝釐，節甫持不可。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered a shrine built within the Forbidden City for Daoist priests to offer prayers, Jiefu held that this could not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered a shrine inside the Forbidden City for Daoist prayers, Jiefu objected.

sentences.zh: 尚書高拱恚甚，遂移疾歸。

translations.literal: Minister Gao Gong was greatly angered; Jiefu thereupon left office citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Gao Gong was furious; Jiefu resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 起光祿丞。

translations.literal: He was later appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 會拱掌吏部，復移疾避之。

translations.literal: When Gong took charge of the Ministry of Personnel, Jiefu again left citing illness to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong took the Ministry of Personnel, Jiefu again resigned to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，屢遷至南京刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the early Wanli years he was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Minister of Punishments in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli he rose to Right Vice Minister of Punishments in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 召為工部左侍郎，攝部事。

translations.literal: Recalled as Left Vice Minister of Works, he acted as head of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Left Vice Minister of Works, he acted as minister.

sentences.zh: 御史高舉言節甫素負難進之節，不宜一歲三遷。

translations.literal: Censor Gao Ju said Jiefu had long borne a reputation for being hard to advance and should not be promoted three ranks in one year.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gao Ju said Jiefu was known as hard to promote and should not rise three ranks in one year.

sentences.zh: 吏部以節甫有物望，絀其議。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel, because Jiefu enjoyed public esteem, rejected the criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel rejected the charge because Jiefu enjoyed public esteem.

sentences.zh: 節甫連上疏請省浮費，核虛冒，止興作，減江、浙織造，停江西瓷器，帝為稍減織造數。
