translations.literal: Jiefu repeatedly memorialized asking to cut floating expenses, audit false claims, halt construction, and reduce Jiangnan textile manufacture and Jiangxi porcelain; the emperor slightly reduced textile quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Jiefu urged cutting waste, auditing fraud, halting construction, and reducing Jiangnan silk and Jiangxi porcelain; the emperor slightly cut silk quotas.

sentences.zh: 中官傳奉，節甫持不可，且上疏言之。

translations.literal: When eunuchs were sent on special commissions, Jiefu held this could not be allowed and memorialized to that effect.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs were given special commissions, Jiefu opposed it in memorial.

sentences.zh: 又嘗獻治河之策，語鑿鑿可用。

translations.literal: He also once submitted a plan for controlling the Yellow River that was solid and practicable.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a Yellow River control plan that was sound and practical.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，卒。

translations.literal: He returned home for mourning for his father and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his father's mourning and died there.

sentences.zh: 贈右副都御史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，㴶方柄用，得賜謚端清。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, when Que was in power, Jiefu was granted the posthumous title Duanqing.
translations.idiomatic: When Que took power in Tianqi, Jiefu received the posthumous title Duanqing.

sentences.zh: 㴶與弟演同登萬曆二年進士。

translations.literal: Que and his younger brother Yan both passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Que and his brother Yan both became jinshi in Wanli 2.

sentences.zh: 㴶改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Que was made a Hanlin academician and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Que became a Hanlin academician and Compiler.

sentences.zh: 累官南京禮部侍郎，掌部事。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Minister of Rites in Nanjing and managed ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Rites in Nanjing and directed the ministry.

sentences.zh: 西洋人利瑪竇入貢，因居南京，與其徒王豐肅等倡天主教，士大夫多宗之。

translations.literal: The Westerner Matteo Ricci came bearing tribute and lived in Nanjing; with his follower Wang Fengsu and others he spread Catholicism, and many scholar-officials followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Matteo Ricci came to Nanjing and, with Wang Fengsu and others, spread Catholicism; many officials followed.

sentences.zh: 㴶奏：「陪京都會，不宜令異教處此。

translations.literal: Que memorialized: "At the capital gathering they ought not to be allowed to dwell here with a foreign faith."
translations.idiomatic: Que memorialized: "They should not be allowed to spread a foreign faith at the capital."

sentences.zh: 」識者韙其言。

translations.literal: Men of insight approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtful men praised him.

sentences.zh: 然㴶素乏時譽。

translations.literal: Yet Que had long lacked contemporary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Que had never enjoyed much reputation.

sentences.zh: 與大學士從哲同里闬，相善也。

translations.literal: He was from the same neighborhood as Grand Secretary Congzhe and they were on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: He was Congzhe's neighbor and ally.

sentences.zh: 神宗末，從哲獨當國，請補閣臣，詔會推。

translations.literal: At the end of Shenzong's reign Congzhe alone held power and asked that Grand Secretaries be supplemented; an edict ordered collective recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Shenzong's reign Congzhe asked to fill the Grand Secretariat; the court ordered recommendations.

sentences.zh: 亓詩教等緣從哲意，擯何宗彥、劉一燝輩，獨以㴶及史繼偕名上。

translations.literal: Qi Shijiao and others, following Congzhe's wish, excluded He Zongyan, Liu Yizao, and others and submitted only Que and Shi Jixie.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shijiao and others, at Congzhe's bidding, blocked He Zongyan and Liu Yizao and nominated only Que and Shi Jixie.

sentences.zh: 帝遂用之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon employed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor used them.

sentences.zh: 或曰由從哲薦也。

translations.literal: Some said it was through Congzhe's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Congzhe had recommended him.

sentences.zh: 疏未發，明年，神宗崩，光宗立，乃召㴶為禮部尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: Before the memorial was issued, the following year Shenzong died and Guangzong ascended; Que was then summoned as Minister of Rites concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Before the memorial went out Shenzong died and Guangzong reigned; Que was summoned as Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 未至，光宗復崩。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Guangzong also died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived Guangzong died too.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年六月，㴶始至。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianqi, Que at last arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 1, sixth month, Que finally arrived.

sentences.zh: 故事，詞臣教習內書堂，所教內豎執弟子禮。

translations.literal: By precedent, Hanlin instructors taught in the Inner Writing Hall and the eunuchs they taught observed disciple ritual.
translations.idiomatic: By custom Hanlin tutors taught eunuchs in the Inner Writing Hall as disciples.

sentences.zh: 李進忠、劉朝皆㴶弟子。

translations.literal: Li Jinxian and Liu Chao were both Que's disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinxian and Liu Chao had both been Que's pupils.

sentences.zh: 李進忠者，魏忠賢始名也。

translations.literal: Li Jinxian was Wei Zhongxian's original name.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinxian was the name Wei Zhongxian first used.

sentences.zh: 㴶既至，密結二人，乃奏言：「遼左用兵亟，臣謹於東陽、義烏諸邑及揚州、纮安募材官勇士二百餘，請以勇士隸錦衣衛，而量授材官職。

translations.literal: When Que arrived he secretly allied with the two and memorialized: "War in Liaodong is urgent; I have recruited over two hundred skilled fighters from Dongyang, Yiwu, Yangzhou, and other places—let the fighters serve in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and grant the skilled men military ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Que secretly allied with them and memorialized recruiting over two hundred fighters for the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 」進忠、朝方舉內操，得㴶奏大喜。

translations.literal: Jinxian and Chao were then promoting inner-court drill and were delighted with Que's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxian and Chao, building inner-court forces, were delighted.

sentences.zh: 詔錦衣官訓練募士，授材官王應鬥等遊擊以下官有差。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Embroidered-Uniform officers to train the recruits and granted Wang Yingdou and others ranks from assault commander downward.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered guard officers to train them and gave Wang Yingdou and others military ranks.

sentences.zh: 㴶又奏募兵後至者復二百餘人，請發遼東、四川軍前。

translations.literal: Que also memorialized that another two hundred-odd recruits had arrived and asked that they be sent to the Liaodong and Sichuan fronts.
translations.idiomatic: Que asked that another two hundred recruits go to Liaodong and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子太保，進文淵閣，再進少保兼太子太保、戶部尚書、武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, entered the Wenyuan Pavilion, and was again promoted to Junior Tutor concurrently Grand Guardian, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Guardian, entered the Wenyuan Pavilion, then Junior Tutor, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 禁中內操日盛，駙馬都尉王昺亦奉詔募兵，願得帷幄重臣主其事。

translations.literal: Inner-court drill daily grew stronger; Commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard Wang Chang also received an edict to recruit troops and wished for a grand minister to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Inner drill grew; Wang Chang also recruited troops and wanted a grand minister in command.

sentences.zh: 廷臣皆言㴶與朝陰相結，於是給事中惠世揚、周朝瑞等劾㴶陽托募兵，陰藉通內。

translations.literal: Court officials all said Que was in secret league with Chao; supervising secretaries Hui Shiyang, Zhou Chaorui, and others impeached Que for openly recruiting troops while secretly communicating within.
translations.idiomatic: Officials said Que colluded with Chao; Hui Shiyang and Zhou Chaorui impeached him for recruiting troops while reaching inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 劉朝內操，㴶使門客誘之。

translations.literal: Liu Chao's inner drill—Que had his retainers entice him.
translations.idiomatic: Que's clients egged on Liu Chao's inner drill.

sentences.zh: 王昺疏，疑出㴶教。

translations.literal: Wang Chang's memorial was suspected to have been dictated by Que.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang's memorial was thought to come from Que.

sentences.zh: 閹人、戚畹、奸輔內外弄兵，長安片土，成戰場矣。

translations.literal: Eunuchs, imperial sons-in-law, and wicked chief ministers played with troops inside and out until a strip of Chang'an became a battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs, in-laws, and wicked ministers armed Chang'an like a battlefield.

sentences.zh: 㴶疏辨，因請疾求罷。

translations.literal: Que memorialized in defense and asked to leave citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Que defended himself and begged to resign on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him and kept him on.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 世揚等遂盡發㴶通內狀，刑部尚書王紀再疏劾㴶，比之蔡京。

translations.literal: Shiyang and others then fully exposed Que's communications within; Minister of Punishments Wang Ji again impeached Que, comparing him to Cai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: They exposed Que's inner dealings; Wang Ji impeached him, comparing him to Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 㴶亦劾紀保護熊廷弼、佟卜年、劉一巘等。

translations.literal: Que also impeached Ji for protecting Xiong Tingbi, Tong Bunian, Liu Yizan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Que impeached Ji for protecting Xiong Tingbi, Tong Bunian, and Liu Yizan.

sentences.zh: 詔兩解之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered both dismissed from the dispute.
translations.idiomatic: An edict told both to stand down.

sentences.zh: 未幾，紀以卜年獄削籍，議者益側目㴶。

translations.literal: Before long Ji was struck from the roster over the Bunian case, and opinion turned still more against Que.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ji was removed over the Bunian case, and opinion turned harder against Que.

sentences.zh: 大學士葉向高言「紀、㴶交攻，均失大臣體。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao said: "Ji and Que attack each other—both fall short of a grand minister's measure.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xianggao said Ji and Que's feud disgraced the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 今以讞獄斥紀，如公論何？

translations.literal: Now to expel Ji over a criminal case—what of public opinion?"
translations.idiomatic: Expelling Ji over a criminal case—what will opinion say?"

sentences.zh: 」朱國祚至以去就爭，帝皆弗聽。

translations.literal: Zhu Guozuo even contested by threatening resignation; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Guozuo threatened to resign; the emperor ignored it.

sentences.zh: 㴶不自安，乃力求去。

translations.literal: Que could not feel secure and strove to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Que, uneasy, pressed to resign.

sentences.zh: 命乘傳歸。

translations.literal: He was ordered home by relay post.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent home by imperial courier.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: More than a year later he died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚文字。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the title Wenzi.

sentences.zh: 㴶弟演，由工部主事歷官南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Que's younger brother Yan rose from Director in the Ministry of Works to Minister of Punishments in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yan rose from a works director to Nanjing Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：神宗之朝，於時為豫，於象為蠱。

translations.literal: The eulogizer says: In Shenzong's reign the time was one of complacency and the omen was decadence.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser writes: Shenzong's age was complacency in time and decadence in omen.

sentences.zh: 時行諸人有鳴豫之兇，而無幹蠱之略。

translations.literal: Shixing and his fellows had the misfortune of complacent clamor but lacked the resource to cure decadence.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing and his like had complacency's ill luck but no cure for decadence.

sentences.zh: 外畏清議，內固恩寵，依阿自守，掩飾取名，弼諧無聞，循默避事。

translations.literal: Outwardly they feared clear opinion, inwardly they clung to favor; they clung to office, masked themselves for reputation, harmonized without effect, and avoided affairs in silence.
translations.idiomatic: They feared public opinion outside, clung to favor within, clung to office, courted reputation, effected no harmony, and dodged affairs in silence.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰「股肱惰哉，萬事隳哉」，此孔子所為致嘆於「焉用彼相」也。

translations.literal: The Book says, 'The limbs are idle—ten thousand affairs are ruined'—this is what Confucius lamented in 'Of what use is that minister?'
translations.idiomatic: The Book says 'The limbs are idle and ten thousand affairs are ruined'—Confucius's sigh at 'Of what use is that minister?'
